translation:
When the World-Honored Buddha had exterminated the evil monkey, he summoned Shakya, Maha Maudgalyayana, and caused them to convert to the Western Paradise of Bliss. Just then, Tianpeng and Tianyou, emerging from the Palace of Precious Dharma in the Divine Apex, exclaimed: "We beg the World-Honored Buddha to delay his departure, our lord's majestic aura has arrived." The Buddha heard their words and turned to gaze in the rear. A brief interval elapsed, and indeed, an Eight-Trigrams Carriage of Auspicious Omens appeared, covered with a Nine-Light Ornamental Dome. Celestial music played a grand symphony of celestial melodies, chanting scriptures beyond reckoning. Flowers of treasure bloomed, wafting true fragrance to the very presence of the Buddha, who expressed gratitude and said: "It is my good fortune that I have practiced the great truth, annihilating evil spirits. I implore the World-Honored Buddha to delay his departure for one day, that the gods and immortals may gather to thank him in one grand banquet."

The World-Honored Buddha could not dare to disobey, and joined his palms to thank the gods, saying: "I am an old monk, who but a mere receptacle of the mandate from the Heavenly King, what power do I possess? It is the Heavenly King and the gods who are blessed with abundance, who have labored to pay their respects." The Jade Emperor decreed an edict, ordering the Cloud Department's retinue of gods to invite, in sequence, the Three Purities, the Four Celestial Attendants, the Five Officials, the Six Origins, the Seven Extremes, the Eight Extremities, the Nine Luminaries, the Ten Capitals, and the myriad saintly worthies to come to the assembly to offer their gratitude to the Buddha. He also commanded the Four Great Celestial Masters and the Nine Heavenly Maiden Immortals to open the Golden Gate of the Jade Capital, the Treasures Palace of the Ultimate Mysterious, and the Jade Pavilion of the Resplendent, to invite the Buddha to ascend the Seven-Jeweled Altar of Spiritual Response. They arranged the seating for each tier, prepared the dragon liver and phoenix marrow, the jade dew and the golden peaches.
source_text: 如来佛祖殄灭了妖猴，即唤傩、迦叶同转西方极乐世界。时有天蓬、天佑急出灵霄宝殿道：“请如来少待，我主大驾来也。”佛祖闻言，回首瞻仰。须臾，果见八景鸾舆，九光宝盖；声奏玄歌妙乐，咏哦无量神章；散宝花，喷真香，直至佛前谢曰：“多蒙大法收殄妖邪。望如来少停一日，请诸仙做一会筵奉谢。”如来不敢违悖，即合掌谢道：“老僧承大天尊宣命来此，有何法力？还是天尊与众神洪福，敢劳致谢？”玉帝传旨，即着云部众神，分头请三清、四御、五老、六司、七元、八极、九曜、十都、千真万圣，来此赴会，同谢佛恩。又命四大天师、九天仙女，大开玉京金阙、太玄宝宫、洞阳玉馆，请如来高坐七宝灵台。调设各班座位，安排龙肝凤髓，玉液蟠桃。
gt_translation: The Tathagata Buddha killed the demon monkey, and immediately called Nuo and Kasyapa to the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss. At that time, Tianpeng and Tianyou rushed out of the Lingxiao Palace and said, "Please stay with the Tathagata a little longer, and my lord will come here." The Buddha heard the words and looked back to pay his respects. In a few moments, I saw the luanyu of eight scenes, the jeweled cover of nine lights; the sound of mystic songs and wonderful music, the chanting of the immeasurable divine chapter; the scattered precious flowers, and the real fragrance, until the Buddha thanked him and said, "I hope that Dafa will save the demons and evil spirits. Stop for a day, and invite all the immortals to do a feast for a while to thank you." The Tathagata did not dare to disobey, so he put his palms together and thanked: "The old monk has come here under the orders of the Great Heavenly Venerate, what is the magic power? ?" The Jade Emperor sent a decree, that is, the gods of the cloud group, separately invited Sanqing, Siyu, Wulao, Liusi, Qiyuan, Baji, Jiuyao, Shidu, and Qianzhen Wansheng to come here to attend the meeting, and thank Buddha's kindness. . He also ordered the Four Heavenly Masters and the Nine Heavens Fairies to open the Jade Palace, the Taixuan Treasure Palace, and the Dongyang Jade Pavilion, and invite the Tathagata to sit on the Qibao Lingtai. Set up the seats of each class, arrange dragon liver and phoenix marrow, jade liquid and peach.

human_translations.translator_1: After the Buddhist Patriarch Tathāgata had vanquished the monstrous monkey, he at once called Ānanda and Kāśyapa to return with him to the Western Paradise. At that moment, however, Tianpeng11 and Tianyou, two celestial messengers, came running out of the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists and said, “We beg Tathāgata to wait a moment, please! Our Lord’s grand carriage will arrive momentarily.” When the Buddhist Patriarch heard these words, he turned around and waited with reverence. In a moment he did indeed see a chariot drawn by eight colorful phoenixes and covered by a canopy adorned with nine luminous jewels. The entire cortege was accompanied by the sound of wondrous songs and melodies, chanted by a vast celestial choir. Scattering precious blossoms and diffusing fragrant incense, it came up to the Buddha, and the Jade Emperor offered his thanks, saying, “We are truly indebted to your mighty dharma for vanquishing that monster. We beseech Tathāgata to remain for one brief day, so that we may invite the immortals to join us in giving you a banquet of thanks.” Not daring to refuse, Tathāgata folded his hands to thank the Jade Emperor, saying, “Your old monk came here at your command, Most Honorable Deva. Of what power may I boast, really? I owe my success entirely to the excellent fortune of Your Majesty and the various deities. How can I be worthy of your thanks?” The Jade Emperor then ordered the various deities from the Thunder Department to send invitations abroad to the Three Pure Ones, the Four Ministers, the Five Elders, the Six Women Officials,12 the Seven Stars, the Eight Poles, the Nine Luminaries, and the Ten Capitals. Together with a thousand immortals and ten thousand sages, they were to come to the thanksgiving banquet given for the Buddhist Patriarch. The Four Great Imperial Preceptors and the Divine Maidens of Nine Heavens were told to open wide the golden gates of the Jade Capital, the Treasure Palace of Primal Secret, and the Five Lodges of Penetrating Brightness. Tathāgata was asked to be seated high on the Numinous Terrace of Seven Treasures, and the rest of the deities were then seated according to rank and age before a banquet of dragon livers, phoenix marrow, juices of jade, and immortal peaches.
human_translations.translator_2: When Lord Buddha had subjugated Monkey, he called on Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the West. Then the immortal heavenly leaders came out of the Lingshao Hall and begged the Buddha to wait a little, till the Jade Emperor arrived. When Buddha heard this, he turned his head and looked up, and there were eight brilliant carriages and nine colored umbrellas, full of choristers singing, praising the Infinite Spirit, and scattering precious fragrant flowers. They came in front of Buddha and said, “Thanks to thy great mercy, the Monkey Demon has been subjugated. Will you not stay a day longer with us so that we may invite all the gods to a thanksgiving banquet?” Lord Buddha put his palms together and thanked them and said, “I came here in obedience to the Jade Emperor. Whatever power has been shown has been owing to his great blessing and all the gods. Please thank him for his kind thought.” Then the Jade Emperor ordered the Board of Thunder and all the gods to arrange themselves, and the Three Pure Ones and the Temple Gods, the Five Elders, the Six Officials and Seven Originals, the Eight Points, the Nine Stars, and the Ten Boards, in all ten thousand sages and saints; and all thank Lord Buddha for his favors. He also ordered the Four Celestial Generals and the Fairies of the Nine Heavens to open the Pearl Palace and the Precious Palace of the Great Mystery and the private rooms and invite Lord Buddha to sit on the top of the seven storied throne, and that seats be arranged for each guest and dishes with dragon livers and phoenix marrow, wine and peaches.
human_translations.translator_4: When he had eliminated the monkey fiend the Buddha told Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the Western paradise. At that moment Tian Peng and Tian You hurried out of the Hall of Miraculous Mist to say, “We beg the Tathagata to wait a moment as the Jade Emperor's chariot is coming.” The Buddha turned round and looked up, and an instant later he saw an eight-splendour imperial chariot and a nine-shining jeweled canopy appear to the sound of strange and exquisite music, and the chanting of countless sacred verses. Precious flowers were scattered and incense was burned. The Jade Emperor went straight up to the Buddha and said, “We are deeply indebted to the great Buddha's powers for wiping out the demon, and we hope that the Tathagata will spend a day here so that we may invite all the Immortals to a feast of thanksgiving.” The Buddha did not dare refuse, so putting his hands together he replied, “This old monk only came here in obedience to Your Celestial Majesty's command. What magic powers can I pretend to? This was all due to the wonderful good fortune of Your Celestial Majesty and the other gods. How could I possibly allow you to thank me?” The Jade Emperor then ordered all the gods of the Department of Thunder to split up and invite the Three Pure Ones, the Four Emperors, the Five Ancients, the Six Superintendents, the Seven Main Stars, the Eight Points of the Compass, the Nine Bright Shiners, the Ten Chiefs, the Thousand Immortals, and the Ten Thousand Sages to a banquet to thank the Buddha for his mercy. Then he ordered the Four Great Heavenly Teachers and the Nine Heavenly Maidens to open the golden gates of the jade capital, and Palace of the Great Mystery, and the Tong Yang Jade Palace, invite the Tathagata to take his seat on the Throne of the Seven Precious Things, arrange the places for all the different groups of guests, and set out the dragon liver, phoenix bone-marrow, jade liquor, and magic peaches.

translation:
As the Buddha Tathagata had just vanquished the demon monkey, He called upon Manjusri and Mahakasyapa to ascend to the Western Pure Land. Just then, the Heavenly Deities of Auspicious Cloud and Protective Blessing suddenly emerged from the Luminous Pavilion and exclaimed, "Please, Lord Buddha, tarry a while, the Jade Emperor is coming." Upon hearing their words, the Buddha turned back to glance behind Him. In a brief moment, behold, an eight-vaned heavenly palanquin appeared, adorned with a nine-rayed umbrella of treasures; divine music played a majestic and enchanting melody, eulogizing the infinite virtues of the Buddha; precious flowers scattered about, wafting the fragrance of truth, and immediately coming to a stop before the Buddha, they bowed in gratitude and said, "We are deeply grateful for Your great Buddhist teachings that have eliminated the wicked demons. We humbly implore the Buddha to stay for just one more day and allow the immortals to offer a feast to express our gratitude." The Tathagata, not daring to disobey the heavenly decree, joined his palms in thanks and said, "The old monk was summoned by the Jade Emperor's command to come here; what power of mine was there? It is the Jade Emperor and the multitudes of gods who possess great fortune, and we dare not presume to thank them." 

The Jade Emperor sent his edict, instructing the cloud department of the heavenly hosts to invite the Three Clarities, the Four Guardians, the Five Officials, the Six Primeval Spirits, the Seven Extremely Talismans, the Eight Extreme Energies, the Nine Planets, the Ten Captains, and the Myriad Sages to come to the gathering to express their gratitude to the Buddha. He also ordered the Four Great Heavenly Masters and the Nine Heavenly Maidens to open the gates of the Jade Capital's Golden Gate, the Supreme Treasures Palace, and the Jade Pavilion of the Sublime Void, and invite the Buddha to ascend to the seven-jewelled spirit altar. Each class was assigned its proper seating arrangement, and the dragon's liver and phoenix marrow were served, along with the nectar of jade and the immortal peaches.
source_text: 如来佛祖殄灭了妖猴，即唤傩、迦叶同转西方极乐世界。时有天蓬、天佑急出灵霄宝殿道：“请如来少待，我主大驾来也。”佛祖闻言，回首瞻仰。须臾，果见八景鸾舆，九光宝盖；声奏玄歌妙乐，咏哦无量神章；散宝花，喷真香，直至佛前谢曰：“多蒙大法收殄妖邪。望如来少停一日，请诸仙做一会筵奉谢。”如来不敢违悖，即合掌谢道：“老僧承大天尊宣命来此，有何法力？还是天尊与众神洪福，敢劳致谢？”玉帝传旨，即着云部众神，分头请三清、四御、五老、六司、七元、八极、九曜、十都、千真万圣，来此赴会，同谢佛恩。又命四大天师、九天仙女，大开玉京金阙、太玄宝宫、洞阳玉馆，请如来高坐七宝灵台。调设各班座位，安排龙肝凤髓，玉液蟠桃。
gt_translation: The Tathagata Buddha killed the demon monkey, and immediately called Nuo and Kasyapa to the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss. At that time, Tianpeng and Tianyou rushed out of the Lingxiao Palace and said, "Please stay with the Tathagata a little longer, and my lord will come here." The Buddha heard the words and looked back to pay his respects. In a few moments, I saw the luanyu of eight scenes, the jeweled cover of nine lights; the sound of mystic songs and wonderful music, the chanting of the immeasurable divine chapter; the scattered precious flowers, and the real fragrance, until the Buddha thanked him and said, "I hope that Dafa will save the demons and evil spirits. Stop for a day, and invite all the immortals to do a feast for a while to thank you." The Tathagata did not dare to disobey, so he put his palms together and thanked: "The old monk has come here under the orders of the Great Heavenly Venerate, what is the magic power? ?" The Jade Emperor sent a decree, that is, the gods of the cloud group, separately invited Sanqing, Siyu, Wulao, Liusi, Qiyuan, Baji, Jiuyao, Shidu, and Qianzhen Wansheng to come here to attend the meeting, and thank Buddha's kindness. . He also ordered the Four Heavenly Masters and the Nine Heavens Fairies to open the Jade Palace, the Taixuan Treasure Palace, and the Dongyang Jade Pavilion, and invite the Tathagata to sit on the Qibao Lingtai. Set up the seats of each class, arrange dragon liver and phoenix marrow, jade liquid and peach.

human_translations.translator_1: After the Buddhist Patriarch Tathāgata had vanquished the monstrous monkey, he at once called Ānanda and Kāśyapa to return with him to the Western Paradise. At that moment, however, Tianpeng11 and Tianyou, two celestial messengers, came running out of the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists and said, “We beg Tathāgata to wait a moment, please! Our Lord’s grand carriage will arrive momentarily.” When the Buddhist Patriarch heard these words, he turned around and waited with reverence. In a moment he did indeed see a chariot drawn by eight colorful phoenixes and covered by a canopy adorned with nine luminous jewels. The entire cortege was accompanied by the sound of wondrous songs and melodies, chanted by a vast celestial choir. Scattering precious blossoms and diffusing fragrant incense, it came up to the Buddha, and the Jade Emperor offered his thanks, saying, “We are truly indebted to your mighty dharma for vanquishing that monster. We beseech Tathāgata to remain for one brief day, so that we may invite the immortals to join us in giving you a banquet of thanks.” Not daring to refuse, Tathāgata folded his hands to thank the Jade Emperor, saying, “Your old monk came here at your command, Most Honorable Deva. Of what power may I boast, really? I owe my success entirely to the excellent fortune of Your Majesty and the various deities. How can I be worthy of your thanks?” The Jade Emperor then ordered the various deities from the Thunder Department to send invitations abroad to the Three Pure Ones, the Four Ministers, the Five Elders, the Six Women Officials,12 the Seven Stars, the Eight Poles, the Nine Luminaries, and the Ten Capitals. Together with a thousand immortals and ten thousand sages, they were to come to the thanksgiving banquet given for the Buddhist Patriarch. The Four Great Imperial Preceptors and the Divine Maidens of Nine Heavens were told to open wide the golden gates of the Jade Capital, the Treasure Palace of Primal Secret, and the Five Lodges of Penetrating Brightness. Tathāgata was asked to be seated high on the Numinous Terrace of Seven Treasures, and the rest of the deities were then seated according to rank and age before a banquet of dragon livers, phoenix marrow, juices of jade, and immortal peaches.

translation: The Buddha Sakyamuni, having annihilated the evil monkey, beckoned the Maitreya and Sariputra to transform and proceed to the Western Pure Land. At that time, Heaven's Imperial Seal, Heaven's Aid, suddenly flew out of the Divine Palace, saying, "Please, Great Buddha, wait a moment, I the Imperial Lord am coming." Upon hearing this, the Buddha turned his head and gazed back. A short while later, indeed a magnificent eight-dragon carriage appeared, adorned with nine-rayed treasure canopies; a heavenly orchestra was playing exquisite music of profound harmony, singing and chanting boundless sacred melodies; scattering precious flowers and wafting true incense, proceeding to offer thanks before the Buddha: "We are deeply grateful to your grand Buddhist law that annihilates evil demons. We beg the Great Buddha to stay for one day, and the gods and immortals to hold a banquet in gratitude." The Buddha dared not to defy, so he joined his hands in thanks, saying, "This humble monk receives the decree of the Supreme Emperor, what authority do I possess? It is the Emperor and the gods who are endowed with boundless blessings, and it is not for us to express gratitude." The Jade Emperor sent down his decree, ordering the Cloud Department and all the gods to separately invite the Three Clarities, the Four Worthy Ones, the Five Emperors, the Six Officers, the Seven Primes, the Eight Extremes, the Nine Celestial Radiance, the Ten Capitals, the Ten Thousand Saints, to come to the gathering to thank the Buddha's blessings. He also commanded the Four Great Heavenly Teachers and the Nine Skies' Goddesses to open the Jade Capital's Golden Gate, the Mysterious Treasure Palace, the Jade Valley Mansion, and invite the Buddha to sit on the seven-jewel sacred platform. He arranged for the seating arrangement, prepared dragon liver and phoenix marrow, jade liquor and peaches.

translation:
When the Buddha of the Past eradicated the demonic monkeys, he summoned Vimalakirti and Mahamoggallana to convert to the Western Pure Land. Just then, Taisui and Tianyou hurriedly emerged from the Spirits' Treasury Palace: "Please wait for a moment, Our Lord is coming." The Buddha heard this and looked back, gazing intently. After a brief moment, he saw a majestic sedan chair with eight auspicious clouds, adorned with a nine-glazed parasol; the sweet music of the heavenly qin resounded, singing celestial tunes without number; scattered flowers of precious jewels, exhaling true fragrance, came to the Buddha and said: "We deeply appreciate the great law of eradication of demonic evil. May the Buddha spare a day, and let us all assemble to pay our respects."

The Buddha, not daring to go against the will of Heaven, folded his hands and said, "The old monk was summoned by the Heavenly Emperor to come here; what is there that I can do? Is it not that the Heavenly Emperor and the multitude of gods are blessed with great good fortune, and dare to repay the Buddha's benevolence?" The Jade Emperor decreed an edict, ordering the cloud spirits and all the gods to, one by one, invite the Three Purities, the Four Observers, the Five Lords, the Six Administrators, the Seven Primal Ones, the Eight Co-Precursors, the Nine Stars, the Ten Capitals, and the Ten Thousand Saints to attend the gathering to thank the Buddha's benevolence. He also instructed the four Great Heavenly Masters and the nine Heavenly Maidens of the Nine Heavens to open the Jade Capital's Golden Barrier, the Treasure Palace of the Supreme Mystery, and the Jade Pavilion of the Sunlit Cave, to invite the Buddha to sit high upon the Seven Treasures Divine Dais. The seating arrangements for the various assemblies were prepared, and arrangements were made for dragon liver and phoenix marrow, and for yao-liquor and jie-fruit.

How can I be worthy of your thanks?” The Jade Emperor then ordered the various deities from the Thunder Department to send invitations abroad to the Three Pure Ones, the Four Ministers, the Five Elders, the Six Women Officials,12 the Seven Stars, the Eight Poles, the Nine Luminaries, and the Ten Capitals. Together with a thousand immortals and ten thousand sages, they were to come to the thanksgiving banquet given for the Buddhist Patriarch. The Four Great Imperial Preceptors and the Divine Maidens of Nine Heavens were told to open wide the golden gates of the Jade Capital, the Treasure Palace of Primal Secret, and the Five Lodges of Penetrating Brightness. Tathāgata was asked to be seated high on the Numinous Terrace of Seven Treasures, and the rest of the deities were then seated according to rank and age before a banquet of dragon livers, phoenix marrow, juices of jade, and immortal peaches.
human_translations.translator_2: When Lord Buddha had subjugated Monkey, he called on Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the West. Then the immortal heavenly leaders came out of the Lingshao Hall and begged the Buddha to wait a little, till the Jade Emperor arrived. When Buddha heard this, he turned his head and looked up, and there were eight brilliant carriages and nine colored umbrellas, full of choristers singing, praising the Infinite Spirit, and scattering precious fragrant flowers. They came in front of Buddha and said, “Thanks to thy great mercy, the Monkey Demon has been subjugated. Will you not stay a day longer with us so that we may invite all the gods to a thanksgiving banquet?” Lord Buddha put his palms together and thanked them and said, “I came here in obedience to the Jade Emperor. Whatever power has been shown has been owing to his great blessing and all the gods. Please thank him for his kind thought.” Then the Jade Emperor ordered the Board of Thunder and all the gods to arrange themselves, and the Three Pure Ones and the Temple Gods, the Five Elders, the Six Officials and Seven Originals, the Eight Points, the Nine Stars, and the Ten Boards, in all ten thousand sages and saints; and all thank Lord Buddha for his favors. He also ordered the Four Celestial Generals and the Fairies of the Nine Heavens to open the Pearl Palace and the Precious Palace of the Great Mystery and the private rooms and invite Lord Buddha to sit on the top of the seven storied throne, and that seats be arranged for each guest and dishes with dragon livers and phoenix marrow, wine and peaches.
human_translations.translator_4: When he had eliminated the monkey fiend the Buddha told Ananda and Kasyapa to return with him to the Western paradise. At that moment Tian Peng and Tian You hurried out of the Hall of Miraculous Mist to say, “We beg the Tathagata to wait a moment as the Jade Emperor's chariot is coming.” The Buddha turned round and looked up, and an instant later he saw an eight-splendour imperial chariot and a nine-shining jeweled canopy appear to the sound of strange and exquisite music, and the chanting of countless sacred verses. Precious flowers were scattered and incense was burned. The Jade Emperor went straight up to the Buddha and said, “We are deeply indebted to the great Buddha's powers for wiping out the demon, and we hope that the Tathagata will spend a day here so that we may invite all the Immortals to a feast of thanksgiving.” The Buddha did not dare refuse, so putting his hands together he replied, “This old monk only came here in obedience to Your Celestial Majesty's command. What magic powers can I pretend to? This was all due to the wonderful good fortune of Your Celestial Majesty and the other gods. How could I possibly allow you to thank me?” The Jade Emperor then ordered all the gods of the Department of Thunder to split up and invite the Three Pure Ones, the Four Emperors, the Five Ancients, the Six Superintendents, the Seven Main Stars, the Eight Points of the Compass, the Nine Bright Shiners, the Ten Chiefs, the Thousand Immortals, and the Ten Thousand Sages to a banquet to thank the Buddha for his mercy. Then he ordered the Four Great Heavenly Teachers and the Nine Heavenly Maidens to open the golden gates of the jade capital, and Palace of the Great Mystery, and the Tong Yang Jade Palace, invite the Tathagata to take his seat on the Throne of the Seven Precious Things, arrange the places for all the different groups of guests, and set out the dragon liver, phoenix bone-marrow, jade liquor, and magic peaches.

translation: When the Tathagata had vanquished the demonic monkey, He summoned Vajra, Mahamoggallana to ascend to the Western Pure Land. At that time, a decree from the Heavens was issued from the Palace of Numinous Radiance, saying, "Please, the Tathagata, wait a moment, my Master has arrived." The Tathagata listened and turned his head to gaze. A brief while later, behold! A majestic sedan chair arrived, its eight dragons in bright array, with a canopy of nine radiant lights. A celestial melody of a sublime and mystic song resounded; incense dispersing divine scriptures; precious flowers blooming, fragrant scents wafting, came to the Buddha's presence to say, "We are deeply grateful to the great Dharma that has vanquished the demonic evil. We beg the Tathagata to wait a day, and all the immortals will gather for a grand feast to offer our gratitude." The Tathagata, not daring to disobey the celestial decree, clasped his hands together in gratitude and said, "This old monk is but obeying the command of the great Celestial Emperor to come here. What power of mine is worthy of being thanked? It is truly the Celestial Emperor and the multitude of gods who are blessed with good fortune. How could I presume to repay your kindness?" The Jade Emperor issued his edict, commanding the multitude of gods of the clouds to invite the Three Pure Ones, the Four Regency Gods, the Five Celestial Guardians, the Six Precepts, the Seven Palaces, the Eight Extremes, the Nine Mysterious Emissaries, the Ten Envoys, and the Thousand True Saints to gather here to offer their gratitude. He also ordered the Four Great Heavenly Teachers and the Nine Heavenly Maidens to open the Jade Capital's Golden Pass, the Pearl of the Great Ultimate, and the Cavern of Jade, to invite the Tathagata to take high seat on the Seven Precious Spirit Platform. The seating was arranged, with each group seated according to their respective order, the Dragon's liver and Phoenix marrow were prepared, and the Jade Elixir of the Peaches of Immortality were laid out.
source_text: 如来佛祖殄灭了妖猴，即唤傩、迦叶同转西方极乐世界。时有天蓬、天佑急出灵霄宝殿道：“请如来少待，我主大驾来也。”佛祖闻言，回首瞻仰。须臾，果见八景鸾舆，九光宝盖；声奏玄歌妙乐，咏哦无量神章；散宝花，喷真香，直至佛前谢曰：“多蒙大法收殄妖邪。望如来少停一日，请诸仙做一会筵奉谢。”如来不敢违悖，即合掌谢道：“老僧承大天尊宣命来此，有何法力？还是天尊与众神洪福，敢劳致谢？”玉帝传旨，即着云部众神，分头请三清、四御、五老、六司、七元、八极、九曜、十都、千真万圣，来此赴会，同谢佛恩。又命四大天师、九天仙女，大开玉京金阙、太玄宝宫、洞阳玉馆，请如来高坐七宝灵台。调设各班座位，安排龙肝凤髓，玉液蟠桃。
gt_translation: The Tathagata Buddha killed the demon monkey, and immediately called Nuo and Kasyapa to the Western Paradise of Ultimate Bliss. At that time, Tianpeng and Tianyou rushed out of the Lingxiao Palace and said, "Please stay with the Tathagata a little longer, and my lord will come here." The Buddha heard the words and looked back to pay his respects. In a few moments, I saw the luanyu of eight scenes, the jeweled cover of nine lights; the sound of mystic songs and wonderful music, the chanting of the immeasurable divine chapter; the scattered precious flowers, and the real fragrance, until the Buddha thanked him and said, "I hope that Dafa will save the demons and evil spirits. Stop for a day, and invite all the immortals to do a feast for a while to thank you." The Tathagata did not dare to disobey, so he put his palms together and thanked: "The old monk has come here under the orders of the Great Heavenly Venerate, what is the magic power? ?" The Jade Emperor sent a decree, that is, the gods of the cloud group, separately invited Sanqing, Siyu, Wulao, Liusi, Qiyuan, Baji, Jiuyao, Shidu, and Qianzhen Wansheng to come here to attend the meeting, and thank Buddha's kindness. . He also ordered the Four Heavenly Masters and the Nine Heavens Fairies to open the Jade Palace, the Taixuan Treasure Palace, and the Dongyang Jade Pavilion, and invite the Tathagata to sit on the Qibao Lingtai. Set up the seats of each class, arrange dragon liver and phoenix marrow, jade liquid and peach.

human_translations.translator_1: After the Buddhist Patriarch Tathāgata had vanquished the monstrous monkey, he at once called Ānanda and Kāśyapa to return with him to the Western Paradise. At that moment, however, Tianpeng11 and Tianyou, two celestial messengers, came running out of the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists and said, “We beg Tathāgata to wait a moment, please! Our Lord’s grand carriage will arrive momentarily.” When the Buddhist Patriarch heard these words, he turned around and waited with reverence. In a moment he did indeed see a chariot drawn by eight colorful phoenixes and covered by a canopy adorned with nine luminous jewels. The entire cortege was accompanied by the sound of wondrous songs and melodies, chanted by a vast celestial choir. Scattering precious blossoms and diffusing fragrant incense, it came up to the Buddha, and the Jade Emperor offered his thanks, saying, “We are truly indebted to your mighty dharma for vanquishing that monster. We beseech Tathāgata to remain for one brief day, so that we may invite the immortals to join us in giving you a banquet of thanks.” Not daring to refuse, Tathāgata folded his hands to thank the Jade Emperor, saying, “Your old monk came here at your command, Most Honorable Deva. Of what power may I boast, really? I owe my success entirely to the excellent fortune of Your Majesty and the various deities. translation: The Jade Emperor, even as he was infuriated and furious, had the Eunuch left and right to speak on his behalf, to strip him of his crown and official title, and to cast him to the battlefield. It was thanks to the timely intervention of the barefoot Heavenly Immortal, who, while reviewing the candidates, rescued me. Although I was to meet with death and be sent to the Eastern Desolate Land, I happened to stumble upon this mountain and took refuge. When I was at my wit's end, I would go hungry and then skip along the waves in search of food. When the woodcutter encountered me, he had no expectation of seeing me again, and when the fisherman laid eyes on my appearance, he shook his head at my miserable condition. Coming and going, countless people devoured others, and rolling and rocking the boat caused me distress. You dare to launch a brutal attack on me, and today my belly has a glimmer of hope. Not knowing how to taste it, you grasp hold of me and say I'm coarse, and that you'll chop me up to make a relish. "You impudent creature, you've completely lost all sense of decorum! I, the old Hog, can still bring up water droplets, how dare you say I'm coarse and need to be chopped up to make a relish! You seem to have taken me for a wily and cunning fellow. Be careful, lest you offend me with your lack of decorum! Eat your ancestral blessings from me!" The monster, seeing the bronze ladle come, made a flapping motion with its wings to avoid it. The two splashed out of the water onto the surface, and each of them climbed up the waves. This battle was unlike the previous one, and look at it: the one wielding the Hanging curtain dagger, the one with the Heavens' Whiskers Standard, each revealed their magical powers, to be admired. That one with the descent-demon-beheading wand, that one with the nine-pronged bronze ladle that moved with incredible speed. Leaping over waves, shaking mountains and rivers, they pushed and turned the world around. The ferocity was as if the Great Year was crashing into the wind-bell, and the evil looked like a deceased person flipping over a treasure box. This one, with a steadfast heart, that one, a guilty one, wreaking havoc as a water monster.
source_text: 玉皇即便怒生嗔，却令掌朝左辅相：卸冠脱甲摘官衔，将身推在杀场上。多亏赤脚大天仙，越班启奏将吾放。饶死回生不典刑，遭贬流沙东岸上。饱时困卧此山中，饿去翻波寻食饷。樵子逢吾命不存，渔翁见我身皆丧。来来往往吃人多，翻翻复复伤生瘴。你敢行凶到我门，今日肚皮有所望。莫言粗糙不堪尝，拿住消停剁鲊酱！”八戒闻言大怒，骂道：“你这泼物，全没一些儿眼色！我老猪还掐出水沫儿来哩，你怎敢说我粗糙，要剁鲊酱！看起来，你把我认做个老走硝哩。休得无礼！吃你祖宗这一钯！”那怪见钯来，使一个凤点头躲过。两个在水中打出水面，各人踏浪登波。这一场赌斗，比前不同，你看那：卷帘将，天蓬帅，各显神通真可爱。那个降妖宝杖着头轮，这个九齿钉钯随手快。跃浪振山川，推波昏世界。凶如太岁撞幛幡，恶似丧门掀宝盖。这一个赤心凛凛保唐僧，那一个犯罪滔滔为水怪。
gt_translation: Even though the Jade Emperor was angry, he ordered his palm towards the left assistant: he took off his crown, took off his armor, took off his official rank, and pushed his body on the killing field. Thanks to the great god of bare feet, Yueban Qisheng released me. Rao back to life without punishment, was banished to the east bank of quicksand. When he is full, he sleeps in this mountain, and when he is hungry, he goes through the waves in search of food and salaries. When the woodcutter meets my life, my life is lost, and the fisherman sees me dead. They come and go to eat a lot of people, and they turn over and over again, and they will suffer from miasmas. If you dare to kill me, there is hope in your belly today. Mo Yan is rough and unpalatable, hold on and chop the scallop sauce! When Bajie heard this, he was furious and scolded, "You bastard, you don't even wink at all!" My old pig is still squeezing water, how dare you say that I am rough and want to chop scallop sauce! It looks like you think of me as an old nerd. Rest is rude! Eat this palladium of your ancestors! "That strange palladium came, so one of the phoenixes nodded to dodge. The two hit the surface in the water, each riding on the waves. This game is different than before. Look at it: the rolling shutter general, the canopy is handsome, They show their supernatural powers so cute. That demon-destroying treasure stick has a head wheel, and this nine-toothed nail palladium is quick and easy. It jumps the waves and shakes the mountains and rivers, and pushes the waves to faint the world. Chi-heartedly protect Tang Seng, that one crime surging as a water monster.

human_translations.translator_1: Hands clasped, he faced his counsel on the left. Stripped of my hat, my armor, and my rank, I had my whole body pushed to the block. Only the Great Immortal, Naked Feet, Came from the ranks and begged to have me freed. Pardoned from death and with my sentence stayed, I was sent to the shores of Flowing-Sand. Sated, I lie wearily in the stream; Famished, I churn the waves to find my feed. The woodsman sees me and his life is gone; The fishers face me and they soon perish. From first to last I’ve eaten many men; Over and over I took human lives. Since you dare to work violence at my door, My stomach this day has its fondest hopes! Don’t say you’re too coarse to be eaten now. I’ll catch you, and look, that’s my minced meat sauce!” Infuriated by what he heard, Eight Rules shouted, “You brazen thing! You haven’t the slightest perception! Old Hog is tempting enough to make people’s mouths water, and you dare say that I’m coarse, that I’m to be chopped up for a chopped meat sauce! Come to think of it, you would like to consider me a piece of tough old bacon! Watch your manners and swallow this rake of your ancestor!” When the monster saw the rake coming, he used the style of “the phoenix nodding its head” to dodge the blow. The two of them thus fought to the surface of the water, each one treading the waters and waves. This conflict was somewhat different from the one before. Look at The Curtain-Raising Captain, The Marshal of Heavenly Reeds: Each showing most nicely his magic might. This one waved above his head the fiend-routing staff: That one moved the rake as swiftly as his hand. The vaulting waves rocked hills and streams; The surging tide the cosmos dimmed. Savage like Jupiter wielding banners and flags! Fierce like Hell’s envoy upsetting sacred tops! This one guarded the Tang Monk devotedly; That one, a water fiend, perpetrated his crimes.
human_translations.translator_3: “We can decide what to do in the morning.” Back inside the cave, the female fiend shook off thoughts of battle and went back to smiling pleasantly. “Make sure the front and back doors are locked,” she ordered her maids, appointing two as sentries to prevent Monkey from sneaking in again. “Light some candles and incense in the bedroom for a bit of ambience,” she told some other servants. “Tonight, Tripitaka and I are going to make beautiful love.” When Tripitaka was delivered to her, she enveloped him in her arms. Dumb with horror, Tripitaka’s instinct was to refuse her, but he worried she might kill him for it. Shaking like jelly, then, he followed her into the fragrant bedroom. By this point, he was too horrified even to hear the fiend’s sweet nothings. The demon began to disrobe, revealing a soft, scented body; Tripitaka wrapped his robe all the more tightly around himself. “I’ll be the courtesan to your emperor,” simpered the fiend. “No, thank you,” he responded. Back and forth they went deep into the night, with Tripitaka staunchly resisting the fiend’s advances. Around midnight, she finally lost her temper, trussed her beloved up like a chicken, ordered her servants to dump him in the corridor, blew out the candles, and shut down the cave for the night. Soon enough, day broke and Monkey got up and stretched. “My headache’s gone,” he rejoiced. “There’s just a little itch left.” “Shall we ask her to give you another tap?” Pigsy teased. “Get lost!” Monkey spat at him. “On the general subject of heads,” continued Pigsy, still in humorous mode, “Master must have let his hair down last night.”
human_translations.translator_4: The Jade Emperor in his terrible fury Put his hands together and fumed to the vice-premier. My hat and armour were removed, and I was stripped of office, Then marched to the place of execution. Then, to my good fortune, the great Bare-foot Immortal Stepped forward to ask for my reprieve. Death was commuted; I was allowed to live In exile on the East bank of the Flowing Sands River. When well-fed I sleep in the river waters; When hungry I burst through the waves in search of food. If a woodcutter meets me his life is finished— No fisherman sees me and survives. In one way and another I've eaten many a man, Cloaked as I am in an aura of death. As you've dared to come to make trouble at my gates My belly has something to look forward to today. No matter if you're coarse and don't taste good, When I've caught you I can cut you up for salted mince.” Pig was extremely angry to hear this, and he replied, “You're completely blind, wretch. I can catch bubbles in my fingers, so how dare you say that I'm so coarse you'll cut me up for salted mince? So you take me to be a very well-cured side of ham! Don't be impudent—take a dose of this rake.” When the monster saw the rake coming at him he did a “phoenix nod” to avoid it. The two of them fought their way up to the surface of the water, where each of them trod on the waves as they struggled in a combat that was even fiercer than their previous one. The Curtain-lifting General, And Marshal Tian Peng; Each gave a splendid show of magic powers. The ogre-quelling staff wheels around the head, The nine-pronged rake is swift in the hand. As they leap on the waves, they shake hills and rivers, Darkening the world as they push the waters aside, As terrible as the Disaster Star striking banners and pendants, As frightening as lifting the canopy off the Death Star. One was the loyal defender of the Tang Priest, The other, a criminal, was an ogre of the waters.

translation: The Jade Emperor may have been enraged, yet he ordered his trusted Minister of the Right to cashier me of my title and post, and cast my body to the execution grounds. Thanks to the timely intervention of the footless heavenly sage, I was pardoned and spared from death, and ended up being banished to the East Bank of the Desert. When I had passed the time and was bedridden in the mountains, I struggled with hunger, rummaging through the bushes for food to eat. Villagers who saw me believed I was a doomed man, fishermen who saw my looks thought I was dead. The more people who came and went, the more I got wounded and sickly. You dare to commit a heinous deed and come to my doorstep, and today I'm finally going to have my belly full. Don't speak with such crude and uncouth speech, and you will be chopped up and turned into pickled sauce!" Hearing this, Eighth Rice Bowl (Bully) flew into a rage and cursed, "You're such a wretch, utterly lacking in dignity! I, old Pig, still have the potency to produce water! How dare you call me crude and say I'll be turned into pickled sauce? It seems you're confusing me for an old long-stemmed garlic plant! Don't be so impolite! I'll deal with you, and it will be the same as chopping your ancestors down!" The fiend saw the sword and dodged with a phoenix-like movement, and then both of them splashed the water's surface, each one jumping onto the waves. This round of combat was different from the previous one – watch how the scroll of mighty powers and the Celestial General Fan each display their divine prowess. The fiend wielding the demonic-slaying rod, the other holding a nine-pronged spear, jump over the waves, send the mountains and rivers into chaos, as calamitous as a Geng Yin (a calamitous sign) tramples on a ceremonial banner, or as vicious as a yokel overturns the treasure cover. This one with his heart beating with righteousness is protecting the Tang Monk, that one wreaking havoc, pouring crimes, serves the water fiend.

Thanks to the great god of bare feet, Yueban Qisheng released me. Rao back to life without punishment, was banished to the east bank of quicksand. When he is full, he sleeps in this mountain, and when he is hungry, he goes through the waves in search of food and salaries. When the woodcutter meets my life, my life is lost, and the fisherman sees me dead. They come and go to eat a lot of people, and they turn over and over again, and they will suffer from miasmas. If you dare to kill me, there is hope in your belly today. Mo Yan is rough and unpalatable, hold on and chop the scallop sauce! When Bajie heard this, he was furious and scolded, "You bastard, you don't even wink at all!" My old pig is still squeezing water, how dare you say that I am rough and want to chop scallop sauce! It looks like you think of me as an old nerd. Rest is rude! Eat this palladium of your ancestors! "That strange palladium came, so one of the phoenixes nodded to dodge. The two hit the surface in the water, each riding on the waves. This game is different than before. Look at it: the rolling shutter general, the canopy is handsome, They show their supernatural powers so cute. That demon-destroying treasure stick has a head wheel, and this nine-toothed nail palladium is quick and easy. It jumps the waves and shakes the mountains and rivers, and pushes the waves to faint the world. Chi-heartedly protect Tang Seng, that one crime surging as a water monster.

human_translations.translator_1: Hands clasped, he faced his counsel on the left. Stripped of my hat, my armor, and my rank, I had my whole body pushed to the block. Only the Great Immortal, Naked Feet, Came from the ranks and begged to have me freed. Pardoned from death and with my sentence stayed, I was sent to the shores of Flowing-Sand. Sated, I lie wearily in the stream; Famished, I churn the waves to find my feed. The woodsman sees me and his life is gone; The fishers face me and they soon perish. From first to last I’ve eaten many men; Over and over I took human lives. Since you dare to work violence at my door, My stomach this day has its fondest hopes! Don’t say you’re too coarse to be eaten now. I’ll catch you, and look, that’s my minced meat sauce!” Infuriated by what he heard, Eight Rules shouted, “You brazen thing! You haven’t the slightest perception! Old Hog is tempting enough to make people’s mouths water, and you dare say that I’m coarse, that I’m to be chopped up for a chopped meat sauce! Come to think of it, you would like to consider me a piece of tough old bacon! Watch your manners and swallow this rake of your ancestor!” When the monster saw the rake coming, he used the style of “the phoenix nodding its head” to dodge the blow. The two of them thus fought to the surface of the water, each one treading the waters and waves. This conflict was somewhat different from the one before. Look at The Curtain-Raising Captain, The Marshal of Heavenly Reeds: Each showing most nicely his magic might. This one waved above his head the fiend-routing staff: That one moved the rake as swiftly as his hand. The vaulting waves rocked hills and streams; The surging tide the cosmos dimmed. Savage like Jupiter wielding banners and flags! Fierce like Hell’s envoy upsetting sacred tops! This one guarded the Tang Monk devotedly; That one, a water fiend, perpetrated his crimes.
human_translations.translator_3: “We can decide what to do in the morning.” Back inside the cave, the female fiend shook off thoughts of battle and went back to smiling pleasantly. “Make sure the front and back doors are locked,” she ordered her maids, appointing two as sentries to prevent Monkey from sneaking in again. “Light some candles and incense in the bedroom for a bit of ambience,” she told some other servants. “Tonight, Tripitaka and I are going to make beautiful love.” When Tripitaka was delivered to her, she enveloped him in her arms. Dumb with horror, Tripitaka’s instinct was to refuse her, but he worried she might kill him for it. Shaking like jelly, then, he followed her into the fragrant bedroom. By this point, he was too horrified even to hear the fiend’s sweet nothings. The demon began to disrobe, revealing a soft, scented body; Tripitaka wrapped his robe all the more tightly around himself. “I’ll be the courtesan to your emperor,” simpered the fiend. “No, thank you,” he responded. Back and forth they went deep into the night, with Tripitaka staunchly resisting the fiend’s advances. Around midnight, she finally lost her temper, trussed her beloved up like a chicken, ordered her servants to dump him in the corridor, blew out the candles, and shut down the cave for the night. Soon enough, day broke and Monkey got up and stretched. “My headache’s gone,” he rejoiced. “There’s just a little itch left.” “Shall we ask her to give you another tap?” Pigsy teased. “Get lost!” Monkey spat at him. “On the general subject of heads,” continued Pigsy, still in humorous mode, “Master must have let his hair down last night.”
human_translations.translator_4: The Jade Emperor in his terrible fury Put his hands together and fumed to the vice-premier. My hat and armour were removed, and I was stripped of office, Then marched to the place of execution. Then, to my good fortune, the great Bare-foot Immortal Stepped forward to ask for my reprieve. Death was commuted; I was allowed to live In exile on the East bank of the Flowing Sands River. When well-fed I sleep in the river waters; When hungry I burst through the waves in search of food. If a woodcutter meets me his life is finished— No fisherman sees me and survives. In one way and another I've eaten many a man, Cloaked as I am in an aura of death. As you've dared to come to make trouble at my gates My belly has something to look forward to today. No matter if you're coarse and don't taste good, When I've caught you I can cut you up for salted mince.” Pig was extremely angry to hear this, and he replied, “You're completely blind, wretch. I can catch bubbles in my fingers, so how dare you say that I'm so coarse you'll cut me up for salted mince? So you take me to be a very well-cured side of ham! Don't be impudent—take a dose of this rake.” When the monster saw the rake coming at him he did a “phoenix nod” to avoid it. The two of them fought their way up to the surface of the water, where each of them trod on the waves as they struggled in a combat that was even fiercer than their previous one. The Curtain-lifting General, And Marshal Tian Peng; Each gave a splendid show of magic powers. The ogre-quelling staff wheels around the head, The nine-pronged rake is swift in the hand. As they leap on the waves, they shake hills and rivers, Darkening the world as they push the waters aside, As terrible as the Disaster Star striking banners and pendants, As frightening as lifting the canopy off the Death Star. One was the loyal defender of the Tang Priest, The other, a criminal, was an ogre of the waters.

translation: The Jade Emperor, even when furious and enraged, ordered the Imperial Censor to remove his crown, strip off his official uniform, and throw him into the execution ground. Luckily, the fierce footless sage Shou Lao had my case taken up and submitted to the court. Although it was a capital offense, I was only exiled to the east coast. When I had spent my days hungry and sick, I took refuge in this mountain, and when I was even hungrier, I rummaged through the sea looking for food to eat. Woodcutters, upon seeing me, thought I was doomed to die, and fishermen, seeing me, thought I was a doomed corpse. People came and went, many eating away at my flesh, and I turned and turned, dodging their bites and trying to protect my life. You dare to come and intimidate me, and today I have a rumbling belly that has something to expect. Don't talk nonsense! If you catch me, I'll be sliced up and pickled in brine! " Upon hearing these words, Zheng Yeren (Monkey King) grew enraged and cursed, "You wretch, you have no sense at all! Even an old pig like me can send up water vapors! How dare you call me coarse and imply I'd be pickled in brine! You seem to think I'm just a coward! Don't be impudent! Eat my ancestral tablet!" The demon saw the tablet coming and dodged it with a phoenix-like gesture. The two of us battled in the water, creating a foamy splash as we each rode the waves onto the boat. This round of combat was unlike the previous one; observe how: the officers who wield the long banners, the heavenly general, each display their divine powers that are truly wonderful. The one wielding the miraculous cudgel has it bobbing on his head, and the other brandishes his nine-toothed iron staff with ease. Jumping over the waves and thrashing the mountains and rivers, stirring up the chaotic world. Fierce like a severe plague sweeping over the banners, treacherous like a demon flinging aside the treasure cover. That one fights with a pure heart, brimming with righteous intent, and this one does evil, recklessly causing chaos as a water demon.

translation:
Jade Emperor though angry and irate, sent off his Grand Minister: remove your cap, strip off your armor, and your title, and thrust your body onto the killing ground. Just in time, the barefooted Great Immortal from the Eastern Sea intervened, sending me to safety. Lest I die, be reborn, and incur an inauspicious punishment, I was banished to the eastern bank of the Drowning Sands. Hunger-stricken, I lay sick on this mountain, and starving, I went to the west to search for food to sustain myself. The woodcutter encountered me with my life in peril, and the fisherman saw that all I have is destruction and withered blight. To come and go, there are many who devour people. To stir and scoop, there is immense destruction of life. You dare to threaten me at my door, today I have hope for something in my stomach. Don't talk nonsense that is too crude to be endured. Take hold and give me a break and mince me into a savory sauce!" 

Hear this, Zhu Bajie blazed with anger, cursing: "You rascal, lacking any finesse whatsoever! My old boar can spit up water bubbles, how dare you say I'm crude, wanting to mince me into a savory sauce! Looking at you, I think you mistake me for some old fool. Do not be impertinent! I'll settle accounts with your ancestors right now!" 

That fiend saw the treasure glint, gave a nod with his phoenix head and dodged out of the way. The two of them plunged into the water and fought on the surface of the water, each one charging and landing on the waves. This fight was different from the previous one, you see: with this monk wielding the whisk of clouds and thunder, the virtues of the divine were manifest. That one grasped the staff of defeating demons, its head rotating rapidly; this one held the iron mace with nine prongs, swift and decisive. Jumping and stirring waves, pushing and bewildering the world. Fierce like a calamitous pestilence crashing into the solar umbra, wicked like the incursion of a defeated and desperate person upending a treasure canopy. That one's red heart blazed in fervent innocence, this one's deeds flowed with abundance, inciting chaos.

Eat your ancestors' pill!" That demon sees the Pole Star halberd, sidesteps with a nod. The two playfully dash the water surface, each tread on the wave and reach the shore.

The one who wields the demon-capturing rod wears it as a crown, the other wields the Nine-Claw Halberd easily at his fingertips. Dancing on the waves, stirring the mountains and rivers, making the world go mad. Fierce like a bad year's cicada-bark axe, evil like a funeral gate knocking over a treasure casket. This one (Tang Seng) steadfastly and intrepidly guards the real Buddhists, the other criminal villainously wants to harm the Water Demon.
source_text: 玉皇即便怒生嗔，却令掌朝左辅相：卸冠脱甲摘官衔，将身推在杀场上。多亏赤脚大天仙，越班启奏将吾放。饶死回生不典刑，遭贬流沙东岸上。饱时困卧此山中，饿去翻波寻食饷。樵子逢吾命不存，渔翁见我身皆丧。来来往往吃人多，翻翻复复伤生瘴。你敢行凶到我门，今日肚皮有所望。莫言粗糙不堪尝，拿住消停剁鲊酱！”八戒闻言大怒，骂道：“你这泼物，全没一些儿眼色！我老猪还掐出水沫儿来哩，你怎敢说我粗糙，要剁鲊酱！看起来，你把我认做个老走硝哩。休得无礼！吃你祖宗这一钯！”那怪见钯来，使一个凤点头躲过。两个在水中打出水面，各人踏浪登波。这一场赌斗，比前不同，你看那：卷帘将，天蓬帅，各显神通真可爱。那个降妖宝杖着头轮，这个九齿钉钯随手快。跃浪振山川，推波昏世界。凶如太岁撞幛幡，恶似丧门掀宝盖。这一个赤心凛凛保唐僧，那一个犯罪滔滔为水怪。
gt_translation: Even though the Jade Emperor was angry, he ordered his palm towards the left assistant: he took off his crown, took off his armor, took off his official rank, and pushed his body on the killing field. Thanks to the great god of bare feet, Yueban Qisheng released me. Rao back to life without punishment, was banished to the east bank of quicksand. When he is full, he sleeps in this mountain, and when he is hungry, he goes through the waves in search of food and salaries. When the woodcutter meets my life, my life is lost, and the fisherman sees me dead. They come and go to eat a lot of people, and they turn over and over again, and they will suffer from miasmas. If you dare to kill me, there is hope in your belly today. Mo Yan is rough and unpalatable, hold on and chop the scallop sauce! When Bajie heard this, he was furious and scolded, "You bastard, you don't even wink at all!" My old pig is still squeezing water, how dare you say that I am rough and want to chop scallop sauce! It looks like you think of me as an old nerd. Rest is rude! Eat this palladium of your ancestors! "That strange palladium came, so one of the phoenixes nodded to dodge. The two hit the surface in the water, each riding on the waves. This game is different than before. Look at it: the rolling shutter general, the canopy is handsome, They show their supernatural powers so cute. That demon-destroying treasure stick has a head wheel, and this nine-toothed nail palladium is quick and easy. It jumps the waves and shakes the mountains and rivers, and pushes the waves to faint the world. Chi-heartedly protect Tang Seng, that one crime surging as a water monster.

human_translations.translator_1: Hands clasped, he faced his counsel on the left. Stripped of my hat, my armor, and my rank, I had my whole body pushed to the block. Only the Great Immortal, Naked Feet, Came from the ranks and begged to have me freed. Pardoned from death and with my sentence stayed, I was sent to the shores of Flowing-Sand. Sated, I lie wearily in the stream; Famished, I churn the waves to find my feed. The woodsman sees me and his life is gone; The fishers face me and they soon perish. From first to last I’ve eaten many men; Over and over I took human lives. Since you dare to work violence at my door, My stomach this day has its fondest hopes! Don’t say you’re too coarse to be eaten now. I’ll catch you, and look, that’s my minced meat sauce!” Infuriated by what he heard, Eight Rules shouted, “You brazen thing! You haven’t the slightest perception! Old Hog is tempting enough to make people’s mouths water, and you dare say that I’m coarse, that I’m to be chopped up for a chopped meat sauce! Come to think of it, you would like to consider me a piece of tough old bacon! Watch your manners and swallow this rake of your ancestor!” When the monster saw the rake coming, he used the style of “the phoenix nodding its head” to dodge the blow. The two of them thus fought to the surface of the water, each one treading the waters and waves. This conflict was somewhat different from the one before. Look at The Curtain-Raising Captain, The Marshal of Heavenly Reeds: Each showing most nicely his magic might. This one waved above his head the fiend-routing staff: That one moved the rake as swiftly as his hand. The vaulting waves rocked hills and streams; The surging tide the cosmos dimmed. Savage like Jupiter wielding banners and flags! Fierce like Hell’s envoy upsetting sacred tops! This one guarded the Tang Monk devotedly; That one, a water fiend, perpetrated his crimes.
human_translations.translator_3: “We can decide what to do in the morning.” Back inside the cave, the female fiend shook off thoughts of battle and went back to smiling pleasantly. “Make sure the front and back doors are locked,” she ordered her maids, appointing two as sentries to prevent Monkey from sneaking in again. “Light some candles and incense in the bedroom for a bit of ambience,” she told some other servants. “Tonight, Tripitaka and I are going to make beautiful love.” When Tripitaka was delivered to her, she enveloped him in her arms. Dumb with horror, Tripitaka’s instinct was to refuse her, but he worried she might kill him for it. Shaking like jelly, then, he followed her into the fragrant bedroom. By this point, he was too horrified even to hear the fiend’s sweet nothings. The demon began to disrobe, revealing a soft, scented body; Tripitaka wrapped his robe all the more tightly around himself. “I’ll be the courtesan to your emperor,” simpered the fiend. “No, thank you,” he responded. Back and forth they went deep into the night, with Tripitaka staunchly resisting the fiend’s advances. Around midnight, she finally lost her temper, trussed her beloved up like a chicken, ordered her servants to dump him in the corridor, blew out the candles, and shut down the cave for the night. Soon enough, day broke and Monkey got up and stretched. “My headache’s gone,” he rejoiced. “There’s just a little itch left.” “Shall we ask her to give you another tap?” Pigsy teased. “Get lost!” Monkey spat at him. “On the general subject of heads,” continued Pigsy, still in humorous mode, “Master must have let his hair down last night.”
human_translations.translator_4: The Jade Emperor in his terrible fury Put his hands together and fumed to the vice-premier. My hat and armour were removed, and I was stripped of office, Then marched to the place of execution. Then, to my good fortune, the great Bare-foot Immortal Stepped forward to ask for my reprieve. Death was commuted; I was allowed to live In exile on the East bank of the Flowing Sands River. When well-fed I sleep in the river waters; When hungry I burst through the waves in search of food. If a woodcutter meets me his life is finished— No fisherman sees me and survives. In one way and another I've eaten many a man, Cloaked as I am in an aura of death. As you've dared to come to make trouble at my gates My belly has something to look forward to today. No matter if you're coarse and don't taste good, When I've caught you I can cut you up for salted mince.” Pig was extremely angry to hear this, and he replied, “You're completely blind, wretch. I can catch bubbles in my fingers, so how dare you say that I'm so coarse you'll cut me up for salted mince? So you take me to be a very well-cured side of ham! Don't be impudent—take a dose of this rake.” When the monster saw the rake coming at him he did a “phoenix nod” to avoid it. The two of them fought their way up to the surface of the water, where each of them trod on the waves as they struggled in a combat that was even fiercer than their previous one. The Curtain-lifting General, And Marshal Tian Peng; Each gave a splendid show of magic powers. The ogre-quelling staff wheels around the head, The nine-pronged rake is swift in the hand. As they leap on the waves, they shake hills and rivers, Darkening the world as they push the waters aside, As terrible as the Disaster Star striking banners and pendants, As frightening as lifting the canopy off the Death Star. One was the loyal defender of the Tang Priest, The other, a criminal, was an ogre of the waters.

translation: 'Mr. Samsa,' the prokurist now called out in a raised voice, 'what's going on? You barricade yourself in your room, only answer with yes and no, cause your parents a great, unnecessary worry, and ignore – by the way – your business obligations in an unheard-of way. I speak in the name of your parents and your boss, and I seriously ask for a clear explanation right away. I'm astonished, I'm astonished. I thought I knew you as a calm and reasonable person, and now it seems you're about to start behaving strangely. Your boss did mention a possible explanation for your absences to me this morning – they concern the debt collection that's been entrusted to you lately – but I swear on my honor that this explanation can't be true. However, I see your inexplicable obstinacy and completely lose any desire to get involved with you in any way. And your position is by no means the most secure. I originally had the intention of saying all this to you privately, but since you're making me waste my time, I don't see why your parents shouldn't know about it. Your recent performance has been very unsatisfactory; we acknowledge that it's not the right time for special deals, we agree on that; but there is no season for not doing any business, Mr. Samsa, and there mustn't be.
source_text: »Herr Samsa,« rief nun der Prokurist mit erhobener Stimme, »was ist denn los? Sie verbarrikadieren sich da in Ihrem Zimmer, antworten bloß mit ja und nein, machen Ihren Eltern schwere, unnötige Sorgen und versäumen – dies nur nebenbei erwähnt – Ihre geschäftlichen Pflichten in einer eigentlich unerhörten Weise. Ich spreche hier im Namen Ihrer Eltern und Ihres Chefs und bitte Sie ganz ernsthaft um eine augenblickliche, deutliche Erklärung. Ich staune, ich staune. Ich glaubte Sie als einen ruhigen, vernünftigen Menschen zu kennen, und nun scheinen Sie plötzlich anfangen zu wollen, mit sonderbaren Launen zu paradieren. Der Chef deutete mir zwar heute früh eine mögliche Erklärung für Ihre Versäumnis an – sie betraf das Ihnen seit kurzem anvertraute Inkasso –, aber ich legte wahrhaftig fast mein Ehrenwort dafür ein, daß diese Erklärung nicht zutreffen könne. Nun aber sehe ich hier Ihren unbegreiflichen Starrsinn und verliere ganz und gar jede Lust, mich auch nur im geringsten für Sie einzusetzen. Und Ihre Stellung ist durchaus nicht die festeste. Ich hatte ursprünglich die Absicht, Ihnen das alles unter vier Augen zu sagen, aber da Sie mich hier nutzlos meine Zeit versäumen lassen, weiß ich nicht, warum es nicht auch Ihre Herren Eltern erfahren sollen. Ihre Leistungen in der letzten Zeit waren also sehr unbefriedigend; es ist zwar nicht die Jahreszeit, um besondere Geschäfte zu machen, das erkennen wir an; aber eine Jahreszeit, um keine Geschäfte zu machen, gibt es überhaupt nicht, Herr Samsa, darf es nicht geben.«
gt_translation: "Mr. Samsa," called the manager with a raised voice, "what's the matter? You're barricading yourself in your room, answering only yes and no, giving your parents serious, needless worries, and, incidentally, neglecting your business responsibilities in an outrageous way. Speaking on behalf of your parents and your boss, I sincerely request an immediate, clear explanation. I'm amazed, I'm amazed. I thought I knew you to be a calm, reasonable person, and now you suddenly seem about to begin parading with strange moods. Although the boss hinted at a possible explanation for your omission this morning - it concerned the debt collection you had recently been entrusted with - I actually gave almost my word of honor that this explanation could not be correct. Now, however, I see your incomprehensible stubbornness and lose all desire to do anything for you. And your position is by no means the strongest. I originally intended to tell you all this in private, but since you're wasting my time here I don't see why your parents shouldn't know it too. So your recent performance has been very unsatisfactory; it is not the season for special business, we recognize that; but there is no such thing as a season when there is no business, Mr. Samsa, there must not be.”

human_translations.translator_1: “Mr. Samsa,” the head clerk now called, raising his voice, “what is the matter? You are barricading yourself in your room, giving only yes and no answers, causing your parents serious and unnecessary concern, and neglecting—I just mention this in passing—your professional responsibilities in an outrageous manner. I am speaking here in the name of your parents and your boss, and I seriously beg you to give a clear and immediate explanation. I am astonished, just astonished. I have always known you to be a quiet, reasonable man and now you suddenly seem to be indulging in rash eccentricities. The Chief did point out a possible explanation for your absence early today—concerning the cash payments that were recently entrusted to you—but in fact I practically gave him my word of honor that this could not be the true explanation. Now, however, I see your incredible obstinacy and have completely lost any desire to intercede on your behalf. And your position is by no means unassailable. I originally intended to speak with you privately, but since you are pointlessly wasting my time, I see no reason why your good parents shouldn’t also hear. Your recent performance has been highly unsatisfactory; it is admittedly not a heavy business season, but a season of no business at all, I assure you, Mr. Samsa, does not exist, cannot exist.”
human_translations.translator_2: ‘Mr. Samsa,’ the manager was now shouting, his voice raised, ‘what’s the matter? You are barricading yourself in your room, answer with only a yes and a no, are making serious and unnecessary troubles for your parents, and neglecting (I mention this only incidentally) your commercial duties in a truly unheard of manner. I am speaking here in the name of your parents and your employer, and I am requesting you in all seriousness for an immediate and clear explanation. I am amazed. I am amazed. I thought I knew you as a calm, reasonable person, and now you appear suddenly to want to start parading around in weird moods. The Chief indicated to me earlier this very day a possible explanation for your neglect—it concerned the collection of cash entrusted to you a short while ago—but in truth I almost gave him my word of honour that this explanation could not be correct. However, now I see here your unimaginable pig headedness, and I am totally losing any desire to speak up for you in the slightest. And your position is not at all the most secure. Originally I intended to mention all this to you privately, but since you are letting me waste my time here uselessly, I don’t know why the matter shouldn’t come to the attention of your parents. Your productivity has also been very unsatisfactory recently. Of course, it’s not the time of year to conduct exceptional business, we recognize that, but a time of year for conducting no business, there is no such thing at all, Mr. Samsa, and such a thing must never be.’
human_translations.translator_3: “Herr Samsa,” the general manager now called out, raising his voice. “What has come over you? You barricade yourself in your room, you reply to queries only with yes and no, you cause your parents onerous, unnecessary worries, and you are neglecting— let me permit myself to note—your professional responsibilities in a truly unprecedented manner. I speak here in the name of your parents as well as your employer and in all seriousness must ask you for a clear and immediate explanation. I am astonished, utterly astonished. I have always known you as a calm, sensible person, and now it seems you’ve begun to permit yourself the most whimsical extravagances. To be sure, the boss did suggest one possible explanation for your absence this morning—it concerns the cash payments recently entrusted to your care—and truthfully, I all but gave him my word of honor that this explanation could not be correct. But confronted here with your incomprehensible obstinacy, I find myself losing any desire I might have had to come to your defense. And your position is anything but secure. It was originally my intention to discuss all this with you in a private conversation, but since you compel me to waste my time here, I do not know why your esteemed parents should not hear of it as well. In short: your productivity of late has been highly unsatisfactory; admittedly this is not the best season for drumming up business, we do acknowledge this; but a season in which no business at all is drummed up is something that does not, and indeed may not exist, Herr Samsa.”

You are barricading yourself in your room, only responding with 'yes' and 'no,' causing your parents unnecessary and serious worry, and for some reason abandoning – I'm just mentioning this in passing – your business duties in an unheard-of manner. I speak on behalf of your parents and your boss, and I'm asking you in all seriousness for a clear and immediate explanation. I am stunned, I am stunned. I thought I knew you to be a calm and reasonable person, but now it seems that you are starting to act strangely with eccentric whims. Our boss hinted at a possible explanation for your absence today – it involved the collection work that has been entrusted to you lately – but I must swear that this explanation is impossible. Now, however, I see your inexplicable stubbornness and have lost all desire to put myself out for you in any way. Your position, after all, is far from secure. I had originally intended to have this conversation with you in private, but since you're making me waste my time here, I don't see why your parents shouldn't also know about it. I am speaking here in the name of your parents and your boss, and I seriously beg you to give a clear and immediate explanation. I am astonished, just astonished. I have always known you to be a quiet, reasonable man and now you suddenly seem to be indulging in rash eccentricities. The Chief did point out a possible explanation for your absence early today—concerning the cash payments that were recently entrusted to you—but in fact I practically gave him my word of honor that this could not be the true explanation. Now, however, I see your incredible obstinacy and have completely lost any desire to intercede on your behalf. And your position is by no means unassailable. I originally intended to speak with you privately, but since you are pointlessly wasting my time, I see no reason why your good parents shouldn’t also hear. Your recent performance has been highly unsatisfactory; it is admittedly not a heavy business season, but a season of no business at all, I assure you, Mr. Samsa, does not exist, cannot exist.”
human_translations.translator_2: ‘Mr. Samsa,’ the manager was now shouting, his voice raised, ‘what’s the matter? You are barricading yourself in your room, answer with only a yes and a no, are making serious and unnecessary troubles for your parents, and neglecting (I mention this only incidentally) your commercial duties in a truly unheard of manner. I am speaking here in the name of your parents and your employer, and I am requesting you in all seriousness for an immediate and clear explanation. I am amazed. I am amazed. I thought I knew you as a calm, reasonable person, and now you appear suddenly to want to start parading around in weird moods. The Chief indicated to me earlier this very day a possible explanation for your neglect—it concerned the collection of cash entrusted to you a short while ago—but in truth I almost gave him my word of honour that this explanation could not be correct. However, now I see here your unimaginable pig headedness, and I am totally losing any desire to speak up for you in the slightest. And your position is not at all the most secure. Originally I intended to mention all this to you privately, but since you are letting me waste my time here uselessly, I don’t know why the matter shouldn’t come to the attention of your parents. Your productivity has also been very unsatisfactory recently. Of course, it’s not the time of year to conduct exceptional business, we recognize that, but a time of year for conducting no business, there is no such thing at all, Mr. Samsa, and such a thing must never be.’
human_translations.translator_3: “Herr Samsa,” the general manager now called out, raising his voice. “What has come over you? You barricade yourself in your room, you reply to queries only with yes and no, you cause your parents onerous, unnecessary worries, and you are neglecting— let me permit myself to note—your professional responsibilities in a truly unprecedented manner. I speak here in the name of your parents as well as your employer and in all seriousness must ask you for a clear and immediate explanation. I am astonished, utterly astonished. I have always known you as a calm, sensible person, and now it seems you’ve begun to permit yourself the most whimsical extravagances. To be sure, the boss did suggest one possible explanation for your absence this morning—it concerns the cash payments recently entrusted to your care—and truthfully, I all but gave him my word of honor that this explanation could not be correct. But confronted here with your incomprehensible obstinacy, I find myself losing any desire I might have had to come to your defense. And your position is anything but secure. It was originally my intention to discuss all this with you in a private conversation, but since you compel me to waste my time here, I do not know why your esteemed parents should not hear of it as well. In short: your productivity of late has been highly unsatisfactory; admittedly this is not the best season for drumming up business, we do acknowledge this; but a season in which no business at all is drummed up is something that does not, and indeed may not exist, Herr Samsa.”

translation: "Mr. Samsa," the procuraist called out loudly, "what is the matter with you? You're barricading yourself in your room, merely responding with yes and no, causing your parents unnecessary worry and – by the way – neglecting your business duties in an unheard-of manner. I'm speaking on behalf of your parents and your boss, and I'm seriously asking for a clear, immediate explanation. I'm astonished, I'm astounded. I thought I knew you as a calm, sensible person, but it seems you're suddenly starting to behave erratically. Our boss did hint this morning that he might have an explanation for your absence, but I genuinely swear that it couldn't be true – you've been entrusted with collecting debts, after all. But now I see your inexplicable obstinacy and completely lose all desire to go to bat for you. Your position is by no means secure. I had initially intended to speak to you privately about this, but since you're wasting my time pointlessly, I see no reason why your parents shouldn't know about it as well. Your performance over the past while has been very unsatisfactory; we acknowledge that it's not the right time for any special business deals, but there's no time for no business at all, Mr. Samsa; it simply cannot be the case."
source_text: »Herr Samsa,« rief nun der Prokurist mit erhobener Stimme, »was ist denn los? Sie verbarrikadieren sich da in Ihrem Zimmer, antworten bloß mit ja und nein, machen Ihren Eltern schwere, unnötige Sorgen und versäumen – dies nur nebenbei erwähnt – Ihre geschäftlichen Pflichten in einer eigentlich unerhörten Weise. Ich spreche hier im Namen Ihrer Eltern und Ihres Chefs und bitte Sie ganz ernsthaft um eine augenblickliche, deutliche Erklärung. Ich staune, ich staune. Ich glaubte Sie als einen ruhigen, vernünftigen Menschen zu kennen, und nun scheinen Sie plötzlich anfangen zu wollen, mit sonderbaren Launen zu paradieren. Der Chef deutete mir zwar heute früh eine mögliche Erklärung für Ihre Versäumnis an – sie betraf das Ihnen seit kurzem anvertraute Inkasso –, aber ich legte wahrhaftig fast mein Ehrenwort dafür ein, daß diese Erklärung nicht zutreffen könne. Nun aber sehe ich hier Ihren unbegreiflichen Starrsinn und verliere ganz und gar jede Lust, mich auch nur im geringsten für Sie einzusetzen. Und Ihre Stellung ist durchaus nicht die festeste. Ich hatte ursprünglich die Absicht, Ihnen das alles unter vier Augen zu sagen, aber da Sie mich hier nutzlos meine Zeit versäumen lassen, weiß ich nicht, warum es nicht auch Ihre Herren Eltern erfahren sollen. Ihre Leistungen in der letzten Zeit waren also sehr unbefriedigend; es ist zwar nicht die Jahreszeit, um besondere Geschäfte zu machen, das erkennen wir an; aber eine Jahreszeit, um keine Geschäfte zu machen, gibt es überhaupt nicht, Herr Samsa, darf es nicht geben.«

translation: The stranger seemed to avoid speaking a lot, but when he did, he spoke in general terms with considerable modesty, and his conversation took on a somewhat bookish tone: that he was an insignificant insect of this world and not worthy of much attention, that he had experienced a great deal in his life, endured much on his service, and had many enemies who had even sought to take his life; and that now, desiring to calm down, he was seeking to find a place to live and, upon arriving in this city, felt it his duty to pay his respects to its highest officials. This was all that was known about this new man in the city, which soon proved itself on the governor's social gathering. The preparations for this gathering took over two hours, and in the guest, there was a fastidiousness with regards to his attire that was rarely seen elsewhere. After a short post-dinner nap, he ordered to be brought a washbasin and, for an incredibly long time, wiped his cheeks with soap, first with the back of his tongue, and then, taking a towel from the shoulder of a tavern servant, he wiped his entire face with it, starting from behind his ears and before giving the tavern servant two hearty slaps in the face. Then, in front of a mirror, he put on a crawat, plucked out two hair from his nose and, immediately after, found himself in a brick-red frock coat with an embroidered scythe. Having thus dressed, he rolled in his own carriage through the city's excessively wide streets, illuminated by the faint light of occasional lamps. However, the governor's house was well-lit, even for a ball; the carriage with lanterns, the two gendarmes at the entrance, the stable lads' cries in the distance – in short, everything was as it should be. Entering the ballroom, Chichikov had to close his eyes for a moment because of the bright light from the candles, lamps, and the ladies' dresses. Everything was illuminated.
