human_translations.translator_1: Now we return to the Devarāja Li and the Third Prince, who, leading the other commanders, went straight to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists to give this report: “By your holy decree your subjects led the expeditionary force down to the Region Below to subdue the baneful immortal, Sun Wukong. We had no idea of his enormous power, and we could not prevail against him. We beseech Your Majesty to give us reinforcements to wipe him out.” “How powerful can we expect one baneful monkey to be,” asked the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are needed?” “May Your Majesty pardon us from an offense worthy of death!” said the prince, drawing closer. “That baneful monkey wielded an iron rod; he defeated first the Mighty-Spirit God and then wounded the shoulder of your subject. Outside the door of his cave he set up a banner bearing the words, ‘The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven.’ He said that if he were given such a rank, he would lay down his arms and come to declare his allegiance. If not, he would fight his way up to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists.” “How dare this baneful monkey be so insolent!” exclaimed the Jade Emperor, astonished by what he had heard. “We must order the generals to have him executed at once!” As he said this, the Gold Star of Venus came forward again from the ranks and said, “The baneful monkey knows how to make a speech, but he has no idea what’s appropriate and what isn’t. Even if reinforcements are sent to fight him, I don’t think he can be subdued right away without taxing our forces. It would be better if Your Majesty were greatly to extend your mercy and proclaim yet another decree of pacification. Let him indeed be made the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven; he will be given an empty title, in short, rank without compensation.” “What do you mean by rank without compensation?” said the Jade Emperor. The Gold Star said, “His name will be Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, but he will not be given any official duty or salary. We shall keep him here in Heaven so that we may put his perverse mind at rest and make him desist from his madness and arrogance. The universe will then be calm and the oceans tranquil again.” Hearing these words, the Jade Emperor said, “We shall follow the counsels of our minister.” He ordered the mandate to be made up and the Gold Star to bear it hence.
human_translations.translator_2: Meanwhile Guardian King Li, had returned with his third son to Heaven, and memorialized thus: “We, your ministers, by your command, led forth an army to subdue the monster the Seeker of Secrets, but as we did not know that his magic power was so great, we did not overcome him. We therefore hope Your Majesty will add more heavenly hosts to destroy him.” The Jade Emperor said, “How can one monkey demon have such ability that you need an additional force?” Then the third son said, “I hope Your Majesty will forgive your minister, and not put him to death. That Monkey Demon had an iron spear with which he first put to flight the Great Victorious Commander. Then he wounded me in my arm. At the entrance of his cave he has hoisted a flag on which is written in large letters “The Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven.” He says if you give him this position and title, he will cease fighting; but if not, he will lay siege to Heaven itself.” The Jade Emperor, hearing this, was much astonished and said, “How dare he be so mad as that?” and ordered all the generals to go and destroy him at once. Just as he spoke, the Minister of Venus stepped out of the ranks and said, “That monkey demon knows how to make big demands, but does not know how far he can go. If you send more heavenly legions to fight him, they will not subdue him easily, so it will cause great trouble to the army. Would it not be better that you should pardon him, and send an edict, granting him the title that he asks? But let it be only an empty title, without any emolument.” The Jade Emperor said, “What do you mean by that?” “Let him come and take up his abode in Heaven,” said the minister, “so that his ambition might be satisfied, and he will no longer create any disturbance, and Heaven and Earth may be at peace again.” The Jade Emperor, having heard this, granted the request. He ordered that an edict be written, and that the Minister of Venus should take it to the Monkey King.
human_translations.translator_3: Meanwhile, King Li and Prince Nezha were reporting on the war to the Jade Emperor. “We were, in truth, surprised by the abilities of this monkey and beg for more soldiers to destroy him.” “How powerful can one monkey be,” wondered the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are required?” “We apologize for our treacherous failure, but this demonic monkey’s iron staff first defeated Mighty-Spirit,” Nezha explained, “then wounded me on the arm.” He next reported Monkey’s demand for a promotion. “Outrageous!” snapped the Jade Emperor. “Have him executed forthwith!” Gold Star now stepped forward. “This baneful monkey knows how to bluster, but not when to stop. I suspect that even if we commit more troops, he won’t be easily defeated, and the campaign will exhaust our armies. Why doesn’t Your Majesty bring him around with another amnesty and give him an honorary title?” “What sort of thing do you have in mind?” the emperor asked. “Let him call himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven—a non-stipendiary post with no duties. That way, we’ll keep him tame and tethered here, and peace will be restored.” “Very well,” agreed the emperor, and dispatched Gold Star with a second amnesty.
human_translations.translator_4: Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha led their forces straight to the Palace of Miraculous Mist and made this request: “We, your subjects, took our forces down to the lower world, under your Divine Edict, to subdue the immortal fiend Sun Wukong. But to our surprise we found that his magical powers were too far-reaching for us to be able to defeat him. We therefore hope that Your Imperial Majesty will send more troops to exterminate him.” “How could a mere monkey goblin have such great powers that you actually need more troops?” asked the Jade Emperor. Prince Nezha then came forward and memorialized, “We beg Your Majesty to spare us the deaths we deserve. That monkey fiend has an iron cudgel that he used to defeat the Mighty Miracle God and wounded me on the shoulder. He has set a banner up outside the entrance to his cave that reads 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' and he says that if you give him this office he will stop fighting and submit; otherwise he will attack the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” When the Jade Emperor heard this he asked in horror, “How dare that monkey fiend talk so wildly? Send all the generals to execute him at once.” As he spoke the Great White Planet stepped forward from the ranks of officials. “That monkey fiend knows how to talk,” he suggested, “but he has no idea about real power. If more soldiers were sent to fight him, they might not be able to overcome him at once and their energies would be wasted. But if Your Imperial Majesty were to show your great mercy, you could send down a pacificatory amnesty and let him be a Great Sage Equaling Heaven. It would only be an empty title that he was given, just an honorary appointment.” “What do you mean by an honorary appointment?” asked the Jade Emperor. “He would be called a Great Sage Equaling Heaven, but he would not be given any responsibility or paid any salary. He would be kept between Heaven and Earth, where his evil nature would be under control and he would be kept from wickedness. Thus Heaven and Earth can be at peace, while sea and sky enjoy tranquillity.” The Jade Emperor approved this suggestion and ordered that a new edict should be issued for the Great White Planet to deliver.

translation: Now, the Li Tian Wang and the Third Prince led the multitude of generals straight to the Palace of Elysium. They kowtowed, saying: "We, your subjects, were dispatched with imperial orders to descend to the mortal realm, capture the evil spirit, the Monkey King Sun Wukong, but he unexpectedly possesses an extraordinary range of magical abilities, and hence our defeat, so we beg Your Majesty to order additional troops to eradicate him." The Jade Emperor said: "Assuming this monkey spirit is as strong as you say, why do you still want to add troops?" The Third Prince stepped forward to speak once more: "We beg Your Majesty to pardon our death sentence! That monkey spirit wields an iron staff, and first defeated the Great Spiritual Being, and then wounded my arm. A staff-bearing banner stands outside the cave entrance, inscribed with four characters: 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven.' It is a decree that bestows upon him that official title, and if we are not granted permission, we will have to assault the Palace of Supreme Treasure itself!" The Jade Emperor, upon hearing this, was astonished and exclaimed: "This monkey spirit dares to be so presumptuous! Order the multitude of generals to immediately put him to death forthwith." Just as he was speaking, a eunuch from the side stepped forward, saying: "The Monkey King only knows how to speak, but not how to gauge the size of the situation. If we launch a military campaign against him, we will not be able to capture him in one go, and instead will be incurring unnecessary losses. I beg Your Majesty to grant Your benevolence, and issue a decree calling for his submission. Let him be given the official title of 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven,' but only in name, without any actual power or authority; he can then be kept in custody to keep his wickedness in check, so as to prevent his conduct from becoming more audacious, thus bringing peace to heaven and earth, and tranquility to the nine seas." The Jade Emperor said: "How do you propose to call this 'having an official title without any power or authority'?" The eunuch replied: "The official title is indeed 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven,' but he won't be in charge of anything, nor will he receive any stipend. Let him be kept in confinement, and his rebellious heart can be tamed, thus preventing him from becoming more arrogant. Thus, the harmony of the universe can be maintained, and the seas and oceans can be kept clear." The Jade Emperor said: "I will follow your suggestion." He then ordered the edict to be issued, and once again entrusted the eunuch to convey it.

The Imperial Commander Li and the Third Prince led the army to the Hall of Elysium. The Imperial Commander Li presented the report, saying: "We were dispatched by imperial order to subjugate the rebel, Sun Wukong. But unexpectedly, his supernatural abilities are far-reaching, and we are unable to defeat him. We hope Your Majesty will increase our troops to destroy him."

The Jade Emperor responded: "You think this evil monkey has how many skills? We need to increase troops?"

The Third Prince approached forward and presented his petition: "I humbly request Your Majesty to pardon my death penalty. This evil monkey wields a iron rod and first defeated the Powerful God, then struck and injured my arm. A banner with the inscription 'Great Saint of Heaven' has been erected outside the gates. It is a formal announcement of his appointment to this office, and he will cease fighting and surrender; if not, he will attack the Palace of the Heavenly Jewel as well."

The Jade Emperor heard this and was astonished, exclaiming: "This evil monkey dares to be so arrogant! Order the generals to kill him at once."

Just then, the former Grand Marshal Tai Bai made an appearance and presented his petition: "The evil monkey only speaks bold words, but does not know what is trivial and what is significant. If we launch an attack and try to subjugate him, we may not be able to do so immediately, and our troops will only be wasted. It would be more merciful if Your Majesty would graciously issue an amnesty edict, and let him take on the title of Great Saint of Heaven. We can just confer on him the empty title, and let him live without a salary or benefits, letting him bask in the fields and mountains, so as to calm his evil thoughts, and thus bring peace and tranquility to the universe."

The Jade Emperor heard this and agreed: "How would you have him called the Great Saint of Heaven?" human_translations.translator_1: Now we return to the Devarāja Li and the Third Prince, who, leading the other commanders, went straight to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists to give this report: “By your holy decree your subjects led the expeditionary force down to the Region Below to subdue the baneful immortal, Sun Wukong. We had no idea of his enormous power, and we could not prevail against him. We beseech Your Majesty to give us reinforcements to wipe him out.” “How powerful can we expect one baneful monkey to be,” asked the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are needed?” “May Your Majesty pardon us from an offense worthy of death!” said the prince, drawing closer. “That baneful monkey wielded an iron rod; he defeated first the Mighty-Spirit God and then wounded the shoulder of your subject. Outside the door of his cave he set up a banner bearing the words, ‘The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven.’ He said that if he were given such a rank, he would lay down his arms and come to declare his allegiance. If not, he would fight his way up to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists.” “How dare this baneful monkey be so insolent!” exclaimed the Jade Emperor, astonished by what he had heard. “We must order the generals to have him executed at once!” As he said this, the Gold Star of Venus came forward again from the ranks and said, “The baneful monkey knows how to make a speech, but he has no idea what’s appropriate and what isn’t. Even if reinforcements are sent to fight him, I don’t think he can be subdued right away without taxing our forces. It would be better if Your Majesty were greatly to extend your mercy and proclaim yet another decree of pacification. Let him indeed be made the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven; he will be given an empty title, in short, rank without compensation.” “What do you mean by rank without compensation?” said the Jade Emperor. The Gold Star said, “His name will be Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, but he will not be given any official duty or salary. We shall keep him here in Heaven so that we may put his perverse mind at rest and make him desist from his madness and arrogance. The universe will then be calm and the oceans tranquil again.” Hearing these words, the Jade Emperor said, “We shall follow the counsels of our minister.” He ordered the mandate to be made up and the Gold Star to bear it hence.
human_translations.translator_2: Meanwhile Guardian King Li, had returned with his third son to Heaven, and memorialized thus: “We, your ministers, by your command, led forth an army to subdue the monster the Seeker of Secrets, but as we did not know that his magic power was so great, we did not overcome him. We therefore hope Your Majesty will add more heavenly hosts to destroy him.” The Jade Emperor said, “How can one monkey demon have such ability that you need an additional force?” Then the third son said, “I hope Your Majesty will forgive your minister, and not put him to death. That Monkey Demon had an iron spear with which he first put to flight the Great Victorious Commander. Then he wounded me in my arm. At the entrance of his cave he has hoisted a flag on which is written in large letters “The Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven.” He says if you give him this position and title, he will cease fighting; but if not, he will lay siege to Heaven itself.” The Jade Emperor, hearing this, was much astonished and said, “How dare he be so mad as that?” and ordered all the generals to go and destroy him at once. Just as he spoke, the Minister of Venus stepped out of the ranks and said, “That monkey demon knows how to make big demands, but does not know how far he can go. If you send more heavenly legions to fight him, they will not subdue him easily, so it will cause great trouble to the army. Would it not be better that you should pardon him, and send an edict, granting him the title that he asks? But let it be only an empty title, without any emolument.” The Jade Emperor said, “What do you mean by that?” “Let him come and take up his abode in Heaven,” said the minister, “so that his ambition might be satisfied, and he will no longer create any disturbance, and Heaven and Earth may be at peace again.” The Jade Emperor, having heard this, granted the request. He ordered that an edict be written, and that the Minister of Venus should take it to the Monkey King.
human_translations.translator_3: Meanwhile, King Li and Prince Nezha were reporting on the war to the Jade Emperor. “We were, in truth, surprised by the abilities of this monkey and beg for more soldiers to destroy him.” “How powerful can one monkey be,” wondered the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are required?” “We apologize for our treacherous failure, but this demonic monkey’s iron staff first defeated Mighty-Spirit,” Nezha explained, “then wounded me on the arm.” He next reported Monkey’s demand for a promotion. “Outrageous!” snapped the Jade Emperor. “Have him executed forthwith!” Gold Star now stepped forward. “This baneful monkey knows how to bluster, but not when to stop. I suspect that even if we commit more troops, he won’t be easily defeated, and the campaign will exhaust our armies. Why doesn’t Your Majesty bring him around with another amnesty and give him an honorary title?” “What sort of thing do you have in mind?” the emperor asked. “Let him call himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven—a non-stipendiary post with no duties. That way, we’ll keep him tame and tethered here, and peace will be restored.” “Very well,” agreed the emperor, and dispatched Gold Star with a second amnesty.
human_translations.translator_4: Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha led their forces straight to the Palace of Miraculous Mist and made this request: “We, your subjects, took our forces down to the lower world, under your Divine Edict, to subdue the immortal fiend Sun Wukong. But to our surprise we found that his magical powers were too far-reaching for us to be able to defeat him. We therefore hope that Your Imperial Majesty will send more troops to exterminate him.” “How could a mere monkey goblin have such great powers that you actually need more troops?” asked the Jade Emperor. Prince Nezha then came forward and memorialized, “We beg Your Majesty to spare us the deaths we deserve. That monkey fiend has an iron cudgel that he used to defeat the Mighty Miracle God and wounded me on the shoulder. He has set a banner up outside the entrance to his cave that reads 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' and he says that if you give him this office he will stop fighting and submit; otherwise he will attack the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” When the Jade Emperor heard this he asked in horror, “How dare that monkey fiend talk so wildly? Send all the generals to execute him at once.” As he spoke the Great White Planet stepped forward from the ranks of officials. “That monkey fiend knows how to talk,” he suggested, “but he has no idea about real power. If more soldiers were sent to fight him, they might not be able to overcome him at once and their energies would be wasted. But if Your Imperial Majesty were to show your great mercy, you could send down a pacificatory amnesty and let him be a Great Sage Equaling Heaven. It would only be an empty title that he was given, just an honorary appointment.” “What do you mean by an honorary appointment?” asked the Jade Emperor. “He would be called a Great Sage Equaling Heaven, but he would not be given any responsibility or paid any salary. He would be kept between Heaven and Earth, where his evil nature would be under control and he would be kept from wickedness. Thus Heaven and Earth can be at peace, while sea and sky enjoy tranquillity.” The Jade Emperor approved this suggestion and ordered that a new edict should be issued for the Great White Planet to deliver.

translation: It was then said that Emperor Li and the Third Prince, accompanied by the countless officials, proceeded straight to the palace of the Heavenly Sage. They presented their petition, saying, "We have been sent by the Imperial Decree to descend to the mortal realm, to subdue the demonical Monkey King, Son of the Heavens. Unbeknownst to us, his supernatural powers are boundless, and he has not been vanquished. We therefore beseech Your Majesty to command the dispatch of more troops to eliminate him." The Jade Emperor replied, "You mean that one mischievous monkey has such great abilities that we need to send more troops to suppress him?" The Third Prince approached closer and petitioned, saying, "We beg Your Majesty to pardon our past transgressions! That mischievous monkey brandished a steel rod, defeated the Great Sage of the Immortals, and even struck my arm. A flag was erected outside the gate, bearing the inscription 'Heaven's Supreme Sage.' It is a warning that he has been granted this title and is thus willing to surrender; if not for this title, he would even dare to strike the palace of the Celestial Treasure." The Jade Emperor heard his words, shocked, and said, "This mischievous monkey dares to be so arrogant! Command the officials to execute him at once." Just as they were speaking, the Star General White Star suddenly appeared from among the assembled officials and petitioned, saying, "That mischievous monkey knows only how to boast, but is unaware of the right and wrong. If we were to engage him in battle, we might not be able to subdue him, and would only be expending troops in vain. I beg Your Majesty to exercise compassion and benevolence, and send a benevolent edict to summon him. Let him be appointed the Heaven's Supreme Sage, but strip him of any power or position, and confine him in the open space between heaven and earth. This would keep his evil heart from concealing its malice and spare us from further anxiety. This would bring peace and tranquility to the world and purify the universe." The Jade Emperor heard his words and replied, "I shall follow your proposal." He immediately issued a decree and ordered White Star to deliver it.

translation:
Speaking of Li Tianwang and the Third Prince leading the generals to the Palace of the Gods, the officials in attendance reported: "We were dispatched by the Imperial Decree to descend into the mortal realm and capture the demonic Monkey, but to our surprise, he was powerful beyond measure, and thus we were unable to overcome him. We humbly request that the Emperor augment our troops in order to eradicate him." The Jade Emperor replied, "How could a demonic monkey possibly have such great abilities? Do we need to augment our troops?" The Prince stepped forward and reported, "I humbly beg for forgiveness for my transgressions! That demonic monkey wields a magical iron rod, and first defeated the Great Spirit, and then injured my arm. A banner stands outside the entrance with the four characters 'Zǐ Tiān Dà Shèng,' saying that he has been conferred this title, and that we should stop our troops and let him surrender; if not, we will batter down the Palace of the Heavenly Treasure." 

The Jade Emperor was shocked and said, "This demonic monkey dares to be so audacious! Order the generals to immediately put him to death." Just then, Tai Bai Jin Xing, from the ranks, suddenly appeared and reported, "The demonic monkey only knows how to boast, but does not comprehend the situation. To deploy troops to fight him would only lead to an unremitting struggle, and our forces would not be able to subdue him in the short term. It would be wise for the Emperor to show mercy and benevolence, and to issue a decree summoning him to submit. Let us just confer on him the title 'Zǐ Tiān Dà Shèng,' but strip him of his authority and not grant him official emoluments. Then, let him live in the void, and let his wickedness be stilled, so that the world may be peaceful and the heavens be clear and serene." The Jade Emperor said, "How should one call him 'with official title but no emoluments'?" Tai Bai Jin Xing replied, "He is called 'Zǐ Tiān Dà Shèng,' but he does not actually have any authority or emoluments, and is simply left to reside in the void. This way, his wickedness will not grow arrogant, and the world will be at peace." The Jade Emperor said, "This is as you have advised. I hereby issue a decree." He then commanded Tai Bai Jin Xing to take it away.

Yu is also very peaceful." The Jade Emperor heard the words and said, "It is according to Qing." He ordered the imperial edict to be sent, and he was still led by Jin Xing.

human_translations.translator_1: Now we return to the Devarāja Li and the Third Prince, who, leading the other commanders, went straight to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists to give this report: “By your holy decree your subjects led the expeditionary force down to the Region Below to subdue the baneful immortal, Sun Wukong. We had no idea of his enormous power, and we could not prevail against him. We beseech Your Majesty to give us reinforcements to wipe him out.” “How powerful can we expect one baneful monkey to be,” asked the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are needed?” “May Your Majesty pardon us from an offense worthy of death!” said the prince, drawing closer. “That baneful monkey wielded an iron rod; he defeated first the Mighty-Spirit God and then wounded the shoulder of your subject. Outside the door of his cave he set up a banner bearing the words, ‘The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven.’ He said that if he were given such a rank, he would lay down his arms and come to declare his allegiance. If not, he would fight his way up to the Treasure Hall of Divine Mists.” “How dare this baneful monkey be so insolent!” exclaimed the Jade Emperor, astonished by what he had heard. “We must order the generals to have him executed at once!” As he said this, the Gold Star of Venus came forward again from the ranks and said, “The baneful monkey knows how to make a speech, but he has no idea what’s appropriate and what isn’t. Even if reinforcements are sent to fight him, I don’t think he can be subdued right away without taxing our forces. It would be better if Your Majesty were greatly to extend your mercy and proclaim yet another decree of pacification. Let him indeed be made the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven; he will be given an empty title, in short, rank without compensation.” “What do you mean by rank without compensation?” said the Jade Emperor. The Gold Star said, “His name will be Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, but he will not be given any official duty or salary. We shall keep him here in Heaven so that we may put his perverse mind at rest and make him desist from his madness and arrogance. The universe will then be calm and the oceans tranquil again.” Hearing these words, the Jade Emperor said, “We shall follow the counsels of our minister.” He ordered the mandate to be made up and the Gold Star to bear it hence.
human_translations.translator_2: Meanwhile Guardian King Li, had returned with his third son to Heaven, and memorialized thus: “We, your ministers, by your command, led forth an army to subdue the monster the Seeker of Secrets, but as we did not know that his magic power was so great, we did not overcome him. We therefore hope Your Majesty will add more heavenly hosts to destroy him.” The Jade Emperor said, “How can one monkey demon have such ability that you need an additional force?” Then the third son said, “I hope Your Majesty will forgive your minister, and not put him to death. That Monkey Demon had an iron spear with which he first put to flight the Great Victorious Commander. Then he wounded me in my arm. At the entrance of his cave he has hoisted a flag on which is written in large letters “The Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven.” He says if you give him this position and title, he will cease fighting; but if not, he will lay siege to Heaven itself.” The Jade Emperor, hearing this, was much astonished and said, “How dare he be so mad as that?” and ordered all the generals to go and destroy him at once. Just as he spoke, the Minister of Venus stepped out of the ranks and said, “That monkey demon knows how to make big demands, but does not know how far he can go. If you send more heavenly legions to fight him, they will not subdue him easily, so it will cause great trouble to the army. Would it not be better that you should pardon him, and send an edict, granting him the title that he asks? But let it be only an empty title, without any emolument.” The Jade Emperor said, “What do you mean by that?” “Let him come and take up his abode in Heaven,” said the minister, “so that his ambition might be satisfied, and he will no longer create any disturbance, and Heaven and Earth may be at peace again.” The Jade Emperor, having heard this, granted the request. He ordered that an edict be written, and that the Minister of Venus should take it to the Monkey King.
human_translations.translator_3: Meanwhile, King Li and Prince Nezha were reporting on the war to the Jade Emperor. “We were, in truth, surprised by the abilities of this monkey and beg for more soldiers to destroy him.” “How powerful can one monkey be,” wondered the Jade Emperor, “that reinforcements are required?” “We apologize for our treacherous failure, but this demonic monkey’s iron staff first defeated Mighty-Spirit,” Nezha explained, “then wounded me on the arm.” He next reported Monkey’s demand for a promotion. “Outrageous!” snapped the Jade Emperor. “Have him executed forthwith!” Gold Star now stepped forward. “This baneful monkey knows how to bluster, but not when to stop. I suspect that even if we commit more troops, he won’t be easily defeated, and the campaign will exhaust our armies. Why doesn’t Your Majesty bring him around with another amnesty and give him an honorary title?” “What sort of thing do you have in mind?” the emperor asked. “Let him call himself Great Sage Equal to Heaven—a non-stipendiary post with no duties. That way, we’ll keep him tame and tethered here, and peace will be restored.” “Very well,” agreed the emperor, and dispatched Gold Star with a second amnesty.
human_translations.translator_4: Heavenly King Li and Prince Nezha led their forces straight to the Palace of Miraculous Mist and made this request: “We, your subjects, took our forces down to the lower world, under your Divine Edict, to subdue the immortal fiend Sun Wukong. But to our surprise we found that his magical powers were too far-reaching for us to be able to defeat him. We therefore hope that Your Imperial Majesty will send more troops to exterminate him.” “How could a mere monkey goblin have such great powers that you actually need more troops?” asked the Jade Emperor. Prince Nezha then came forward and memorialized, “We beg Your Majesty to spare us the deaths we deserve. That monkey fiend has an iron cudgel that he used to defeat the Mighty Miracle God and wounded me on the shoulder. He has set a banner up outside the entrance to his cave that reads 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' and he says that if you give him this office he will stop fighting and submit; otherwise he will attack the Hall of Miraculous Mist.” When the Jade Emperor heard this he asked in horror, “How dare that monkey fiend talk so wildly? Send all the generals to execute him at once.” As he spoke the Great White Planet stepped forward from the ranks of officials. “That monkey fiend knows how to talk,” he suggested, “but he has no idea about real power. If more soldiers were sent to fight him, they might not be able to overcome him at once and their energies would be wasted. But if Your Imperial Majesty were to show your great mercy, you could send down a pacificatory amnesty and let him be a Great Sage Equaling Heaven. It would only be an empty title that he was given, just an honorary appointment.” “What do you mean by an honorary appointment?” asked the Jade Emperor. “He would be called a Great Sage Equaling Heaven, but he would not be given any responsibility or paid any salary. He would be kept between Heaven and Earth, where his evil nature would be under control and he would be kept from wickedness. Thus Heaven and Earth can be at peace, while sea and sky enjoy tranquillity.” The Jade Emperor approved this suggestion and ordered that a new edict should be issued for the Great White Planet to deliver.

translation: Just as they were drinking and celebrating, someone came to report: "Great King, there are two horned ghost kings waiting outside to see the Great King." The Monkey King said, "Let them in." That ghost king straightened his clothes and rushed into the cave, bowing down on the ground. The Monkey King asked him, "Why have you come to see me?" The ghost king replied, "I have long heard of the Great King calling for the talented, but never managed to meet him; today I see the Great King conferring the Heavenly Canon, and I am overjoyed to return with great honor; I have specially presented a piece of cinnabar-yellow robes to the Great King to celebrate. I dare not be rejected as a humble person; if I am taken in, I can render the service of an ass or a horse." The Monkey King was greatly pleased, put on the cinnabar-yellow robes, and the others were delighted to form a line and bow in reverence; he then appointed the ghost king as the Commander-in-Chief and the Vanguard. After the ghost king had expressed his gratitude and finished speaking, he said, "The Great King has been in heaven for a long time, what office has he been entrusted with?" The Monkey King said, "The Jade Emperor favors the talented and has appointed me to the position of what 'Equine Servitor'!" The ghost king listened and then said, "The Great King has such divine power, how can he care for horses? Why not be appointed as the 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven'?" The Monkey King heard this and was overjoyed beyond measure, exclaiming repeatedly, "Good! Good! Good!" He instructed his four brave generals: "Hurry and make a pennant with the four characters 'Great Sage Equal to Heaven,' set up the pole and hang it up. From now on, I am only to be called the Great Sage Equal to Heaven, and not to be called the Great King. This decree should also be sent to all the ghost kings of the various caves, so that they know about it."

human_translations.translator_1: As they were drinking wine and conversing happily, someone came to report: “ Great King, there are two one-horned demon kings outside who want to see you.” “Show them in,” said the Monkey King. The demon kings straightened out their attire, ran into the cave, and prostrated themselves. “Why did you want to see me?” asked the Handsome Monkey King. “We have long heard that the Great King is receptive to talents,” said the demon kings, “but we had no reason to request your audience. Now we learn that our Great King has received a divine appointment and has returned in success and glory. We have come, therefore, to present the Great King with a red and yellow robe for his celebration. If you are not disdainful of the uncouth and the lowly and are willing to receive us plebeians, we shall serve you as dogs or as horses.” Highly pleased, the Monkey King put on the red and yellow robe while the rest of them lined up joyfully and did homage. He then appointed the demon kings to be the Vanguard Commanders, Marshals of the Forward Regiments. After expressing their thanks, the demon kings asked again, “Since our Great King was in Heaven for a long time, may we ask what kind of appointment he received?” “The Jade Emperor belittles the talented,” said the Monkey King. “He only made me something called the BanHorsePlague.” Hearing this, the demon kings said again, “Great King has such divine powers! Why should you take care of horses for him? What is there to stop you from assuming the rank of the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven?” When the Monkey King heard these words, he could not conceal his delight, shouting repeatedly, “Bravo! Bravo!” “Make me a banner immediately,” he ordered the four mighty commanders, “and inscribe on it in large letters, ‘The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven.’ Erect a pole to hang it on. From now on, address me only as the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, and the title Great King will no longer be permitted. The Monster Kings of the various caves will also be informed so that it will be known to all.” Of this we shall speak no further.
human_translations.translator_2: Whilst they were drinking wine together, there came in a man, who said, “Great King, at our gate there are two one horned kings, who wish to see you.” The Monkey King said, “Let them come in.” The two kings outside straightened their clothes, entered the cave, kowtowed and said, “We have long heard of the Great King who is in search of worthy officials, but we had no opportunity of meeting him before. Now we have heard that the Great King has been given a post in heaven. He must be pleased, and have come back with honors. So we have come to present him with a yellow robe as a token of congratulation. If he will kindly accept it, please let him use it as he does his horses and dogs.” The Monkey King was very pleased, put on the yellow robe and appointed the demon kings as viceroys under him. Having thanked him for his favor, the demon kings said, “You were in heaven a long time, what rank did you occupy there?” The Monkey King replied, “The Jade Emperor did not respect me, and simply appointed me to look after some horses.” The demon kings said, “Since you, Great King, have marvelous magic powers, how did you submit to merely looking after horses? If you had called yourself the Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven, there would have been nothing you could not have done.” The Monkey King was delighted beyond measure on hearing this, and could not refrain from repeating, “Good, Good, Good!” several times. He ordered his four generals to make him a banner on which was to be written in large letters, “The Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven.” He put up a tall flagstaff and hoisted the banner, and cried, “Henceforth never again call me the Great King, but the Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven. Report this to all the demon chiefs, so that they may know.” The day after the Monkey King had left his post in heaven, when the court was about to assemble, the Master of Ceremonies brought in the two assistant grooms instead of the Horse Master. They knelt before the throne and said, “We beg to say that the new Horse Master, not satisfied with the low position assigned to him, has left Heaven altogether.”
human_translations.translator_3: In the middle of the banquet, two visitors were announced: a pair of rhinoceros-horned demon kings. As soon as Monkey had them shown in, they rushed up to prostrate themselves. “Having heard about your Heavenly appointment and that you’d returned covered in glory, we wish to congratulate you with this red and yellow robe and to offer our faithful service.” Monkey happily slipped on the robe, accepted the adulation of the entire banqueting hall, and appointed the demon kings his frontline commanders. “Just as a matter of interest, what post did Heaven give you?” the new arrivals asked. “That crummy Jade Emperor made me his groom,” grumbled Monkey. “What?” The demon kings seemed astonished. “How could an omnipotent magic monkey be made to look after horses? You are the Great Sage Equal to Heaven!” Monkey thought this was the best thing ever. “Quick as you can,” he ordered his generals, “make me a flag saying ‘The Great Sage Equal to Heaven’ and mount it on a bamboo pole. No more of this ‘Great King’ rubbish. And tell my brothers the monstrous monarchs, too.” * * * • • •
human_translations.translator_4: As they were drinking someone came in to report, “Your Majesty, there are two Single-horned Devil Kings outside who want to see you.” “Ask them in,” said the Monkey King, and the two formally-dressed devil kings hurried into the cave and prostrated themselves. “Why have you come to see me?” asked the Handsome Monkey King; and they replied, “We have long heard that Your Majesty is looking for men of talent, but we were unable to see you before. Now that Your Majesty has been given heavenly office and come back in triumph, we would like to offer you this yellow robe as a token of our congratulations. We also hope that you will not reject us although we are low and worthless, but will accept our humble services.” An exultant Monkey King put on the yellow robe and his happy subjects bowed to him in order of precedence. The two devil kings were appointed Commanders of the Van, and when they had thanked the Monkey King for this they asked, “What office did Your Majesty hold while you were all that time in Heaven?” “The Jade Emperor has no respect for talent,” replied the Monkey King. “He made me something called 'Protector of the Horses.'” “Your Majesty has such miraculous powers: you should never have been feeding his horses for him. You should have been made a 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' shouldn't you?” The Monkey King was beside himself with delight at this suggestion, and he kept saying how splendid it was. “Get me a banner made at once with the words 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven' in big letters on it, and put up a pole to hang it from,” he ordered his four Stalwart Generals. “From now on I am to be called 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' not 'Your Majesty' or 'King'. Pass this order on to all the other kings of the monsters.” We will leave him at this point.

translation:
As they were drinking and feasting together, someone came to report, "The Great King, there are two horned kings of ghosts at the door, asking to see the Great King." The Monkey King said, "Let them come in." The horned king came in, hurriedly removing his coat and bowing to the ground. The Monkey King asked him, "What brings you here to see me?" The horned king replied, "I have long heard that the Great King is recruiting talent and haven't had the chance to meet him. Today, having been granted the Heavenly Classic, I've returned in triumph and come to offer a piece of cinnabar-colored robes as a gift, to celebrate with the Great King. Would you deign to take in a humble man, and allow me to render my services like a dog or a horse?"

The Monkey King was overjoyed and put on the cinnabar-colored robes. The assembly stood in line and bowed respectfully to pay their homage. Thereupon, the Monkey King promoted the horned king to the position of Commander-in-Chief and Vanguard. The horned king expressed his gratitude, and then asked, "Great King, it's been a long time since You've been in heaven, what position were You given?" The Monkey King replied, "The Jade Emperor has slighted You and gave me the title of 'Protector of Horses'!" The horned king then said, "With Your supernatural abilities, how could You possibly tend horses? Why not just give Yourself the title of 'Supreme Sage of Heaven'?" The Monkey King heard this and was overjoyed, saying "Good! Good! Good!" and ordered the four sturdy generals, "Quickly set up a banner with the four characters 'Supreme Sage of Heaven,' and raise it on a pole to hang there. From now on, I'll be known as the Supreme Sage of Heaven and won't be called the Great King again. You may also spread this to the various cave-dwelling demons, so that they'll all know."

translation:
Just as they were drinking and feasting together, someone came to report: "Great King, there are two Horned Goblin Kings outside who want to see the Great King." The Monkey King said, "Let them in." The goblin king hastily ran into the cave, and then bowed on his face to the ground. The Monkey King asked him, "What business do you have with me?" The goblin king said, "For a long time I've heard of the Great King's call for the talented, yet I've never had the chance to see him; today I see that the Great King has taken possession of the Heavenly Script, and I'm full of joy and gratitude. I'd like to offer a cassia yellow robe to the Great King, to express my congratulations. If you don't reject this lowly person, and instead receive me, I'll be able to repay your kindness by performing the labor of a dog or a horse." 

The Monkey King was overjoyed and put on the cassia yellow robe. All the others greeted him with reverence and lined up to pay their respects, and the Monkey King then appointed the goblin king as the Front Commander-in-Chief Vanguard. The goblin king finished his thank-yous, then asked, "Your Majesty, the Heavenly Script has been bestowed on you for a long time. What position has Your Majesty been given?" The Monkey King said, "The Jade Emperor has promoted me to some insignificant 'Arhat-protecting-the-horses.'" The goblin king heard this and then added, "Your Majesty has such divine abilities, how could you be in charge of raising horses? Why not just call yourself 'Equal to Heaven Great Sage' instead?" 

The Monkey King heard this and was filled with joy beyond words, and several times said "Excellent! Excellent! Excellent!" He ordered his four mighty generals, "Quickly set up a pennant for me, and on it write the four characters 'Equal to Heaven Great Sage.' Plant the pole and hang it up. We have come, therefore, to present the Great King with a red and yellow robe for his celebration. If you are not disdainful of the uncouth and the lowly and are willing to receive us plebeians, we shall serve you as dogs or as horses.” Highly pleased, the Monkey King put on the red and yellow robe while the rest of them lined up joyfully and did homage. He then appointed the demon kings to be the Vanguard Commanders, Marshals of the Forward Regiments. After expressing their thanks, the demon kings asked again, “Since our Great King was in Heaven for a long time, may we ask what kind of appointment he received?” “The Jade Emperor belittles the talented,” said the Monkey King. “He only made me something called the BanHorsePlague.” Hearing this, the demon kings said again, “Great King has such divine powers! Why should you take care of horses for him? What is there to stop you from assuming the rank of the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven?” When the Monkey King heard these words, he could not conceal his delight, shouting repeatedly, “Bravo! Bravo!” “Make me a banner immediately,” he ordered the four mighty commanders, “and inscribe on it in large letters, ‘The Great Sage, Equal to Heaven.’ Erect a pole to hang it on. From now on, address me only as the Great Sage, Equal to Heaven, and the title Great King will no longer be permitted. The Monster Kings of the various caves will also be informed so that it will be known to all.” Of this we shall speak no further.
human_translations.translator_2: Whilst they were drinking wine together, there came in a man, who said, “Great King, at our gate there are two one horned kings, who wish to see you.” The Monkey King said, “Let them come in.” The two kings outside straightened their clothes, entered the cave, kowtowed and said, “We have long heard of the Great King who is in search of worthy officials, but we had no opportunity of meeting him before. Now we have heard that the Great King has been given a post in heaven. He must be pleased, and have come back with honors. So we have come to present him with a yellow robe as a token of congratulation. If he will kindly accept it, please let him use it as he does his horses and dogs.” The Monkey King was very pleased, put on the yellow robe and appointed the demon kings as viceroys under him. Having thanked him for his favor, the demon kings said, “You were in heaven a long time, what rank did you occupy there?” The Monkey King replied, “The Jade Emperor did not respect me, and simply appointed me to look after some horses.” The demon kings said, “Since you, Great King, have marvelous magic powers, how did you submit to merely looking after horses? If you had called yourself the Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven, there would have been nothing you could not have done.” The Monkey King was delighted beyond measure on hearing this, and could not refrain from repeating, “Good, Good, Good!” several times. He ordered his four generals to make him a banner on which was to be written in large letters, “The Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven.” He put up a tall flagstaff and hoisted the banner, and cried, “Henceforth never again call me the Great King, but the Great Sage, the Equal of Heaven. Report this to all the demon chiefs, so that they may know.” The day after the Monkey King had left his post in heaven, when the court was about to assemble, the Master of Ceremonies brought in the two assistant grooms instead of the Horse Master. They knelt before the throne and said, “We beg to say that the new Horse Master, not satisfied with the low position assigned to him, has left Heaven altogether.”
human_translations.translator_3: In the middle of the banquet, two visitors were announced: a pair of rhinoceros-horned demon kings. As soon as Monkey had them shown in, they rushed up to prostrate themselves. “Having heard about your Heavenly appointment and that you’d returned covered in glory, we wish to congratulate you with this red and yellow robe and to offer our faithful service.” Monkey happily slipped on the robe, accepted the adulation of the entire banqueting hall, and appointed the demon kings his frontline commanders. “Just as a matter of interest, what post did Heaven give you?” the new arrivals asked. “That crummy Jade Emperor made me his groom,” grumbled Monkey. “What?” The demon kings seemed astonished. “How could an omnipotent magic monkey be made to look after horses? You are the Great Sage Equal to Heaven!” Monkey thought this was the best thing ever. “Quick as you can,” he ordered his generals, “make me a flag saying ‘The Great Sage Equal to Heaven’ and mount it on a bamboo pole. No more of this ‘Great King’ rubbish. And tell my brothers the monstrous monarchs, too.” * * * • • •
human_translations.translator_4: As they were drinking someone came in to report, “Your Majesty, there are two Single-horned Devil Kings outside who want to see you.” “Ask them in,” said the Monkey King, and the two formally-dressed devil kings hurried into the cave and prostrated themselves. “Why have you come to see me?” asked the Handsome Monkey King; and they replied, “We have long heard that Your Majesty is looking for men of talent, but we were unable to see you before. Now that Your Majesty has been given heavenly office and come back in triumph, we would like to offer you this yellow robe as a token of our congratulations. We also hope that you will not reject us although we are low and worthless, but will accept our humble services.” An exultant Monkey King put on the yellow robe and his happy subjects bowed to him in order of precedence. The two devil kings were appointed Commanders of the Van, and when they had thanked the Monkey King for this they asked, “What office did Your Majesty hold while you were all that time in Heaven?” “The Jade Emperor has no respect for talent,” replied the Monkey King. “He made me something called 'Protector of the Horses.'” “Your Majesty has such miraculous powers: you should never have been feeding his horses for him. You should have been made a 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' shouldn't you?” The Monkey King was beside himself with delight at this suggestion, and he kept saying how splendid it was. “Get me a banner made at once with the words 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven' in big letters on it, and put up a pole to hang it from,” he ordered his four Stalwart Generals. “From now on I am to be called 'Great Sage Equaling Heaven,' not 'Your Majesty' or 'King'. Pass this order on to all the other kings of the monsters.” We will leave him at this point.

translation: He walked for a long time down the long and narrow corridor, finding no one, and he was about to shout loudly when, in a dark corner between the old wardrobe and the door, he noticed some strange object, something that seemed to be alive. He bent down with a candle and saw a child - a girl no more than five years old, soaked, like a torn rag, in her dripping dress, shuddering and crying. She didn't seem to be frightened by Svidrigailov, but looked at him with dull amazement in her big black eyes, and occasionally sobbed like a child who has cried for a long time, has stopped, and then suddenly starts sobbing again. Her little face was pale and exhausted; she was numb from the cold, but 'how did she end up here? Probably she hid herself here and didn't sleep all night.' He started to question her. The girl suddenly perked up and quickly, rapidly babbled something to him in her child's language. There was something about 'mama' and that 'mama will beat' and some cup she 'shattered' (broke). The girl spoke without stopping; one could somehow guess from all these stories that this was a neglected child, whom a mother, probably a permanently drunk cook from the local inn, had beaten and intimidated; that the girl had broken her mother's cup and that she was so scared that she had run away the evening before; that she had probably hidden somewhere in the yard, in the rain, and finally slipped in here, hiding behind the wardrobe, and sat there in the corner all night, crying, shuddering from the dampness, from the darkness, and from fear that they would now punish her severely for it. He picked her up, went to his room, put her on the bed, and started undressing her. Her holey little shoes, on her bare foot, were so wet as if they had lain all night in a puddle. Undressing her, he put her in bed, covered and wrapped her up completely in a blanket. She fell asleep at once. Having finished, he again became gloomy and pensive.
source_text: Он долго ходил по всему длинному и узкому коридору, не находя никого, и хотел уже громко кликнуть, как вдруг в темном углу, между старым шкафом и дверью, разглядел какой-то странный предмет, что-то будто бы живое. Он нагнулся со свечой и увидел ребенка – девочку лет пяти, не более, в измокшем, как поломойная тряпка, платьишке, дрожавшую и плакавшую. Она как будто и не испугалась Свидригайлова, но смотрела на него с тупым удивлением своими большими черными глазенками и изредка всхлипывала, как дети, которые долго плакали, но уже перестали и даже утешились, а между тем нет-нет и вдруг опять всхлипнут. Личико девочки было бледное и изнуренное; она окостенела от холода, но «как же она попала сюда? Значит, она здесь спряталась и не спала всю ночь». Он стал ее расспрашивать. Девочка вдруг оживилась и быстро-быстро залепетала ему что-то на своем детском языке. Тут было что-то про «мамасю» и что «мамася плибьет», про какую-то чашку, которую «лязбиля» (разбила). Девочка говорила не умолкая; кое-как можно было угадать из всех этих рассказов, что это нелюбимый ребенок, которого мать, какая-нибудь вечно пьяная кухарка, вероятно из здешней же гостиницы, заколотила и запугала; что девочка разбила мамашину чашку и что до того испугалась, что сбежала еще с вечера; долго, вероятно, скрывалась где-нибудь на дворе, под дождем, наконец пробралась сюда, спряталась за шкафом и просидела здесь в углу всю ночь, плача, дрожа от сырости, от темноты и от страха, что ее теперь больно за все это прибьют. Он взял ее на руки, пошел к себе в нумер, посадил на кровать и стал раздевать. Дырявые башмачонки ее, на босу ногу, были так мокры, как будто всю ночь пролежали в луже. Раздев, он положил ее на постель, накрыл и закутал совсем с головой в одеяло. Она тотчас заснула. Кончив все, он опять угрюмо задумался.

human_translations.translator_2: He spent a long time pacing the long, narrow corridor, without finding anyone. He was about to shout for someone when he caught sight of a strange shape, something that seemed to be alive, in a dark corner between an old wardrobe and a door. He bent down with his candle and saw a child—a girl aged no more than five, wearing a little frock soaked through like a wet dishrag. She was shivering and crying. She didn’t seem frightened of Svidrigailov, but just stared at him in dull surprise, with her big dark eyes, uttering a sob from time to time, as a child does when it has been crying for a long time but has stopped and even calmed down, and yet may suddenly start sobbing again any minute. Her little face was pale and exhausted, and she was stiff with cold. ‘How ever did she get here? She must have hidden here and slept through the whole night!’ He began asking her questions. The girl livened up and lisped something in a hurried, childish voice. She chattered on without stopping; it appeared from her tales that she was an unloved child, whom her mother, some sort of a cook who was permanently drunk, and probably worked in this very hotel, had beaten and terrified; the girl had broken Mamasha’s cup and had been so frightened that she’d run away early in the evening; no doubt she’d spent ages hiding somewhere out in the yard, in the rain, and eventually crept in here and hidden behind the cupboard, where she’d crouched in the corner all night, crying, shivering from the damp and the darkness and her terror of being cruelly beaten for what she’d done. He lifted her in his arms and carried her back to his room, sat her on the bed and undressed her. The torn little shoes on her bare feet were as wet as if they’d been lying in a puddle all night. human_translations.translator_3: He walked for some time through a long narrow corridor without finding anyone and was just going to call out, when suddenly in a dark corner between an old cupboard and the door he caught sight of a strange object which seemed to be alive. He bent down with the candle and saw a little girl, not more than five years old, shivering and crying, with her clothes as wet as a soaking house-flannel. She did not seem afraid of Svidrigailov, but looked at him with blank amazement out of her big black eyes. Now and then she sobbed as children do when they have been crying a long time, but are starting to be comforted. The child’s face was pale and tired, she was numb with cold. “How can she have come here? She must have hidden here and not slept all night.” He began questioning her. The child suddenly became animated, chattered away in her baby language, something about “Mother” and that “Mother would beat her,” and about some cup that she had “bwoken.” The child chattered on without stopping. He could only guess from what she said that she was a neglected child, whose mother, probably a drunken cook, in the service of the hotel, whipped and frightened her; that the child had broken a cup of her mother’s and was so frightened that she had run away the evening before, had hidden for a long while somewhere outside in the rain, at last had made her way in here, hidden behind the cupboard and spent the night there, crying and trembling from the damp, the darkness and the fear that she would be badly beaten for it. He took her in his arms, went back to his room, sat her on the bed, and began undressing her. The torn shoes which she had on her stockingless feet were as wet as if they had been standing in a puddle all night. When he had undressed her, he put her on the bed, covered her up and wrapped her in the blanket from her head downwards. She fell asleep at once. Then he sank into dreary musing again.
